title: First-person (in-head) view is decoupled from the character: Q/E turns do not rotate the view and mouse-X does not turn the character
decomp_evidence: CameraSet::SetInHead acclient.c:149230: SetTranslationalStiffness(1.0), SetTargetDirection((0,1,0)) and viewer_offset (0,0.18,0) in the pivot frame. CameraManager::UpdateCamera builds pivot_frame from the player's frame or plane direction (`Position::localtoglobalvec((Position*)&v8[6], ..., &v3->direction)`). So the in-head eye and look direction follow the player heading, damped only by r_stiffness. CameraSet::Rotate acclient.c:148788, in-head branch (offset == (0,0.18,0)): `headinga = CPhysicsObj::get_heading(v18); v19 = headinga + 8.0;` (:148903), then cmdinterp TurnToHeading, i.e. the CHARACTER turns 8 degrees per step. With m_UseMouseTurning it issues TurnRight/TurnLeft 0x6500000D/0x6500000E (:148942). CameraSet::MouseLookHandler :149300-149340 sends mouse X into Rotate(..., camera_keys=0).
openac_evidence: RetailChaseCamera.cs:134 ComputeInHeadPose(pivotWorld, heading, ...) uses the player-yaw heading, and :525 places the eye at `pivotWorld + headingForward * RetailFirstPersonForward`. RetailChaseCamera.cs:258-260: AdjustYaw in head does `_pendingFirstPersonRotate += adjustment`. CameraFrameController.cs:113 and :146-153 pass this to TryTakeFirstPersonTurn, then RequestTurnToHeading(heading +/- 8 degrees). Tests: RetailChaseCameraTests.cs:1000 AdjustYawInFirstPerson_StaysInTheHeadAndAsksTheCharacterToTurn and :778 SecondUpdate_FirstPerson_SnapsTranslationAndOnlyDampsRotation.
holt_evidence: camera.js:1707-1708 `_positionInHead(p) { const fx = Math.sin(this.followYaw);` builds both the eye offset and the look direction from followYaw. camera.js:1084 `if (this._retailZoomOn && this._inHead) return; // first-person: yaw = look dir` turns off auto-follow in head. camera.js:887 right-drag only does `this.followYaw += mx * POINTER_YAW_SENS * ...`. Movement is player-local (camera.js computeMovementFromKeys, 'WASD now drives in the player's local body frame').
discrepancy: In holtburger first person, turning with Q/E rotates the body but leaves the view fixed. Mouse-X drag swings the view but not the body, so after looking around, W walks in a different direction from where you are looking. The 0.18 m eye offset also follows the free yaw, not the head. In retail the in-head view is rigidly tied to the player heading (rotation damped by stiffness), and mouse or rotate input turns the character in 8 degree TurnToHeading steps.
proposed_change: In _positionInHead, take the yaw from the character: `const yaw = this._playerHeadingForFollow() ?? this.followYaw;`. Write it back to this.followYaw so that leaving the head keeps continuity. Use it for both the eye offset (IN_HEAD_FORWARD_M) and the look vector. Keep followPitch and clampInHeadDirZ for vertical look. In onMouseMove (camera.js:~887), when `this._retailZoomOn && this._inHead`, do not add to followYaw. Instead accumulate `mx * POINTER_YAW_SENS * this._mouseSensMult`. Each time the accumulator passes 8 degrees (0.13963 rad), call `sessionHandle.turnToHeading(pose.heading -/+ 0.13963)` and subtract the step. The sign follows followYaw = -pose.heading: dragging right lowers pose.heading. turnToHeading uses the CCW pose.heading convention, the same as headingFromTurnQuat in scene3d/server_turn.js. Optional: when camStiffness is set, slerp only the in-head ROTATION, as retail keeps r_stiffness while t_stiffness = 1. Put the pure step logic in camera_math.js (`inHeadTurnSteps(accum) -> {steps, rest}`).
test_plan: node apps/holtburger-web/tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs. (1) Pure tests for inHeadTurnSteps: an accumulator of 0.2 rad gives 1 step and a remainder of 0.0604; a negative accumulator gives negative steps; the step equals 8 degrees. (2) Static source assertions: _positionInHead calls _playerHeadingForFollow, and the onMouseMove in-head branch calls turnToHeading and does not add to followYaw. The existing assertion `_positionInHead\(p\);\s*\n\s*return;` still holds.

verify.reasons: Holtburger side, re-read: camera.js:1707-1709 `_positionInHead(p) { const fx = Math.sin(this.followYaw);` builds both the eye offset and the look vector from followYaw. camera.js:1084 `if (this._retailZoomOn && this._inHead) return;` turns auto-follow off in head. The only writers of followYaw are camera.js:887 (right-drag), :1102 (autofollow) and index.js:7475 (a wire-agent debug hook). `_retailZoomNotch` (:1830-1837) does not re-seed followYaw on entering the head. retailCamZoom is default-on (`!== "off"`, :570). computeMovementFromKeys (:2425-2490) is player-local, so in first person Q/E turn the hidden body while the view stays fixed, and W walks along the body heading, not the view. Decomp, re-read: CameraSet::SetInHead (acclient.c:149230) calls SetTranslationalStiffness(1.0) and SetTargetDirection((0,1,0)) and sets offset (0,0.18,0). SetTargetForOffset (:148214) sets ALIGN_WITH_PLANE|LOOK_IN_DIRECTION for that offset. CameraManager::UpdateCamera (:147425) builds pivot_frame from the player's frame and direction, so the in-head eye and view follow the heading. CameraSet::Rotate (:148788), in-head branch (taken when !m_UseMouseTurning || camera_keys): `headinga = CPhysicsObj::get_heading(v18); v19 = headinga + 8.0` and then cmdinterp TurnToHeading; the 2013 pseudo-C (line 97230+) names the slot `TurnToHeading`. CameraSet::MouseLookHandler (:149264) calls Rotate(..., keep_going=0, ..., camera_keys=0) once mouselook_x_extent > 5. OpenAC citations check out: RetailChaseCamera.cs:134 and :525, :258-260 `_pendingFirstPersonRotate += adjustment`, CameraFrameController.cs:113 TryTakeFirstPersonTurn and TurnForFirstPersonRotate, and tests :778 and :1000. Not tracked: HANDOFF-openac-comparison-2026-10-08.md lists camera-1 only as an unverified round-2 claim, and PARITY-STATUS.json has no camera item. Why only partial: the proposed mouse-turn mechanism is wrong and would break running. sessionHandle.turnToHeading (lib.rs `turn_to_heading`, line ~39646) enqueues PursuitTurnToHeading. That uses `MovementParameters::default()` (params.rs:67 DEFAULT_MOVEMENT_BITFIELD 0x1EE0F, which includes stop_completely 0x10000). move_to.rs:610 sets `pending_entry_stop = params.stop_completely()`. The pursuit-install arm in system.rs (~4805-4822) also sets `self.active_drive = None` when a manual drive is held. So every mouse step while holding W would stop the run or take the drive away. Retail CommandInterpreter::TurnToHeading (acclient.c:718082) does `params.bitfield &= 0xFFFEFFFF` (clears stop_completely), speed 1.0, hold_key 2 if run, so retail keeps running while turning.
verify.corrections: (1) The step semantics are not retail. Retail and OpenAC issue ONE TurnToHeading(current_heading +/- 8 deg) per rotate event (retail: per mouse event after a 5-event debounce; OpenAC: once per frame while a rotate is pending). The turn amount is re-targeted from the CURRENT heading and rate-limited by the character's turn speed, not proportional to mouse distance. The proposed accumulator of 1 step per 8 deg of mouse yaw is a holtburger invention. (2) The existing turnToHeading export cannot be reused. It stops the player completely and takes over a held WASD drive (above), whereas retail CommandInterpreter::TurnToHeading clears stop_completely. A new wasm entry with retail CommandInterpreter semantics is required, so needs_wasm_rebuild=true. (3) Read the heading through frame_pose.js readLocalPlayerPose (one wasm crossing per frame, commit 48f84780), not another direct getLocalPlayerPose.
verify.implementation_notes: Part A, JS only: in _positionInHead take `yaw = headingFromPose ?? this.followYaw`, where headingFromPose = -readLocalPlayerPose(handle).heading (followYaw = -pose.heading, per the AUTOFOLLOW doc block at camera.js:219-240). Write it back to this.followYaw for continuity on exit. Use it for the IN_HEAD_FORWARD_M offset and the look vector; keep followPitch and clampInHeadDirZ. Part B needs Rust: add `turnToHeadingRetail(heading_rad, run)` (lib.rs, next to turnToHeading) through a SessionCommand. It must build MovementParameters with `bitfield &= !0x1_0000`, speed 1.0, and hold_key_to_apply = 2 when run (CommandInterpreter::TurnToHeading :718082). It must not null a held Manual active_drive: skip the system.rs pursuit-install `self.active_drive = None` arm for this variant, or route it so the turn node composes with the held forward command. In camera.js onMouseMove, when `_retailZoomOn && _inHead`, do not add mx to followYaw. Latch a sign, and once per frame (in tick) while |pending| > 0 call turnToHeadingRetail(poseHeading -/+ 8 deg in radians) (drag right = pose.heading decreases), then clear pending. Optionally mirror the 5-event mouselook_x_extent debounce. Pure helper in camera_math.js: `firstPersonTurnTarget(poseHeadingRad, pendingSign)`, returning the target wrapped to (-pi, pi], or null when pendingSign is 0. Ship Part A and Part B together: Part A alone removes horizontal mouse-look in first person. Escape flag `?inHeadTurn=off` (default-on, `!== "off"`, row in docs/url-flags.md). Tests: node tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs. Add pure cases for firstPersonTurnTarget (sign, +/-pi wrap, 8 deg = 0.13963 rad). Add a static assertion that _positionInHead reads readLocalPlayerPose and that the in-head onMouseMove branch does not write followYaw. Keep the existing `_positionInHead\(p\);\s*\n\s*return;` assertion (line 189). Rust #[test] in crates/holtburger-core movement tests: the retail turn variant leaves a held Manual drive's forward intact and does not set pending_entry_stop. The orchestrator runs cargo and wasm-pack.

title: Collision runs before smoothing and the view is aimed from the collided eye; retail smooths toward the uncollided pose, then sweeps, and keeps the sought orientation
decomp_evidence: SmartBox::PlayerPhysicsUpdatedCallback acclient.c:144049 calls `CameraManager::UpdateCamera(cm, &result, &this->viewer)`: it interpolates FROM the collided viewer (`Frame::interpolate_origin(&actual_pos.frame, &v9->frame, &camera_frame, t_frac)` :147841, `interpolate_rotation(... r_frac)` :147842; frac = stiffness*quantum*10). The target is the UNCLIPPED camera_frame (:147763 pivot_frame.localtoglobal(viewer_offset); orientation set at :147799 from target_direction, which is the heading, or pivot minus the unclipped origin under LOOK_AT_PIVOT :147767). The result becomes viewer_sought_position. SmartBox::update_viewer :144991 then sweeps pivot to sought with init_object(player, 92 = IS_VIEWER|PATH_CLIPPED|FREE_ROTATE|PERFECT_CLIP) (:145086) and publishes `set_viewer(&sphere_path.curr_pos)` (:145091). FREE_ROTATE snaps curr_pos orientation to end_pos up front (ported in holtburger-dat driver_validate.rs:378-384). Net effect: collision only moves the eye position, pull-in is immediate, re-extension is damped, and the view direction never depends on the collided eye. Default stiffness is 0.45 (CameraManager ctor :147898, 1055286886 = 0.45f).
openac_evidence: RetailChaseCamera.cs:151-164: `candidateEye = Vector3.Lerp(_publishedEye, targetEye, tAlpha)` (from the published, i.e. swept, eye toward the unclipped target), then `CollisionProbe.SweepEye(pivotWorld, _soughtEye, ...)`. :176 uses the damped forward from the unclipped pose: `CreateLookAt(publishedEye, publishedEye + _dampedForward, Z)`. Tests: RetailChaseCameraTests.cs:1493 Update_AfterClampReleases_EyeReExtendsGradually, :1542 Update_SweepTargetConvergesOntoContact_NotTheFullBoom, :1646 Update_PressedAgainstWall_EyeGlidesStably. CameraDiagnostics.cs:18/20 default stiffness is 0.45.
holt_evidence: camera.js:1313 `const camera = this._clipCameraAgainstWorld(p, finalX, finalY, finalZ);` runs first. With stiffness set, camera.js:1382 `_applyStiffness(dt, finalX, ...)` lerps persp.position toward the CLIPPED target (:1749-1766). The hard-lock default is camera.js:1385 `this.persp.lookAt(...acToThree(lookX, lookY, lookZ))` from the clipped eye, with lookZ = p.z + 1.6 + lookLift (:1335). The guardLookHorizontal LIVE-03 patch (:1369) exists because a clipped eye can land on the head and give a vertical look vector. The camera_settings.js DEFAULTS comment says stiffness 1.0 is kept on purpose.
discrepancy: (a) Hard-lock default: when an occluder clears (a pillar, doorframe or tree passes), the eye jumps back out by up to 6 m in one frame. Retail re-extends at about 7.5% per frame at 60 Hz. (b) When the eye is pulled in, its look vector to the fixed lookAt point steepens. At the default pitch of 0.3, a 30% pull-in tilts the view from about 22 degrees to about 42 degrees down, and a full pull-in gives the degenerate vertical basis. Retail's view direction does not change under collision. (c) With ?camStiffness or a user-set stiffness, the camera lerps from its old position (now behind the wall) toward the clipped target, so it spends about 0.5 s on the far side of geometry. Retail's sweep runs after the lerp, so the published eye is always valid.
proposed_change: Restructure the follow branch of positionCamera. (1) Compute the ideal eye and the look point, including cast-bias, as today. Set `fwd = normalize(look - ideal)`: this is the sought orientation, independent of collision. (2) Smooth the POSITION before the sweep: `tFrac = stiffnessFrac(this._camStiffness ?? 1, dt)`, `sought = seeded && |prev - ideal| < STIFFNESS_TELEPORT_SNAP_M ? lerp(this._prevEyeAc, ideal, tFrac) : ideal`. (3) `eye = this._clipCameraAgainstWorld(p, sought...)`, then `this._prevEyeAc = eye` (in AC coordinates). (4) Publish `persp.position = acToThree(eye)` with orientation from `Matrix4.lookAt(eye, eye + fwd, up)`, slerped by rFrac when stiffness is set. Remove `_applyStiffness`'s position lerp toward the clipped target. Keep guardLookHorizontal as a backstop; it becomes inert because fwd comes from the ideal eye. Put the pure step in camera_math.js as `retailViewerStep(prevEye, idealEye, frac, sweepFn)`. Follow-up for the owner to decide (feel default): set the Camera-tab stiffness default to retail 0.45 instead of 1.0 (camera_settings.js DEFAULTS).
test_plan: node apps/holtburger-web/tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs. Add pure cases for retailViewerStep that mirror the OpenAC tests, using a fake sweep that clamps at x = -1. (a) Frame 1 publishes on the wall plane, never beyond it. (b) After the wall is removed, the next eye moves only frac (4.5*dt) of the way out. (c) While pressed against the wall, the per-frame delta over 30 frames is under 1e-3. (d) With frac = 1 (hard-lock), sought equals ideal. (e) The forward vector is identical with and without the clamp. Update the static assertions at lines ~248-260 that pin `_applyStiffness(dt, finalX` so they pin the new ordering: the sweep call appears after the lerp.
already_tracked: no (the LIVE-03 guardLookHorizontal patch treats one symptom; camera_settings.js documents the hard-lock default as deliberate)

verify.reasons: Decomp, re-read: SmartBox::PlayerPhysicsUpdatedCallback (acclient.c:144042) calls `CameraManager::UpdateCamera(this->camera_manager, &result, &this->viewer)` and stores the result as viewer_sought_position. In UpdateCamera (:147425) camera_frame.origin is `pivot_frame.localtoglobal(viewer_offset)`, the UNCLIPPED origin. Under LOOK_AT_PIVOT (target_status & 4) the direction is `delta - camera_frame.m_fOrigin`, again from the unclipped origin. The function then does `Frame::interpolate_origin(&actual_pos.frame, &v9->frame, &camera_frame, normal.x)` with v9 = this->viewer (the previously SWEPT eye) and frac = t_stiffness*quantum*10, forced to 1 when stiffness > 1-2e-4. SmartBox::update_viewer (:144991) then sweeps pivot to sought with init_object(player, 92) (92 = 0x5C = IS_VIEWER|PATH_CLIPPED|FREE_ROTATE|PERFECT_CLIP, acclient.h:6180) and calls set_viewer(curr_pos). The ctor sets t_stiffness and r_stiffness to 1055286886 = 0.45f (:147898-147899). OpenAC RetailChaseCamera.cs:153 lerps `_publishedEye` toward targetEye, :164 sweeps, :176 uses `_dampedForward`; tests :1493, :1542 and :1646 exist. Holtburger, re-read: camera.js:1313 clips first. :1382 `_applyStiffness(dt, finalX...)` lerps persp.position (the previous published, never swept) toward the CLIPPED target (:1749-1766). The hard-lock path (:1384-1385) calls lookAt(lookX, lookY, lookZ) from the clipped eye, with lookZ = p.z + 1.6 + lookLift (:1335). guardLookHorizontal (:1369) patches the t=0 degenerate case. Claim (b) holds: with lookLift != 0 the look point is not on the head-to-eye sweep line (start p.z+1.6, :1525), so a pull-in along the segment changes the view direction. In retail the clipped eye lies on the pivot-to-sought line, so looking at the pivot is invariant. Claim (c) holds whenever stiffness < 1 (?camStiffness or the Camera tab). No existing fix: `git log` shows no reorder, and no PARITY-STATUS item covers it.
verify.corrections: (a) is not a divergence under the owner's default. At stiffness 1.0, retail's frac is also forced to 1 (`if t_stiffness <= 1-2e-4 ... else v60=1; frac=1`), so retail re-extends in one frame too. The gradual re-extension only exists at stiffness < 1, so drop (a) or fold it into (c). The tilt numbers are off. With followPitch 0.3 and distance 6 (camera.js:438-439), the ideal view is 22.3 deg down. 41.7 deg is reached with the eye at 30% of the boom (a 70% pull-in); a 30% pull-in gives about 26.5 deg. Ordering detail for holtburger: compute the sought orientation AFTER the step-1 terrain clamp. If fwd comes from the pre-clamp ideal, a terrain-raised eye on an uphill keeps a fixed forward and the player drops low in the frame. That clamp is a holtburger approximation retail does not have (see camera-3). guardLookHorizontal must test the ideal eye XY, not the clipped finalX/finalY.
verify.implementation_notes: In positionCamera's follow branch (camera.js ~1286-1400): (1) Compute idealX/Y/Z as today, then apply the outdoor terrain floor to the ideal; move step 1 of _clipCameraAgainstWorld out, or split it into `_terrainFloorIdeal`. (2) Compute look (lookX/lookY/lookZ, cast-bias included). Keep `let lookX = p.x, lookY = p.y` verbatim, because tests/test_c1_facing_camera.cjs:208 pins it. Run guardLookHorizontal on (idealX, idealY) against look, then set fwd = normalize(look - ideal). (3) tFrac = this._camStiffness != null ? stiffnessFrac(this._camStiffness, dt) : 1. sought = (seeded && |prevEyeAc - ideal| <= STIFFNESS_TELEPORT_SNAP_M && tFrac < 1) ? lerp(prevEyeAc, ideal, tFrac) : ideal. (4) eye = sweeps(head to sought), steps 2-6 only, then this._prevEyeAc = eye in AC coordinates. Reset _prevEyeAc wherever _stiffSeeded is reset (in-head exit, __setCamStiffness, mode switch). (5) persp.position = acToThree(eye). Target quaternion from Matrix4.lookAt(acToThree(eye), acToThree(eye+fwd), up); slerp persp.quaternion by rFrac (same stiffnessFrac) when stiffness is set, otherwise copy. Drop _applyStiffness's position lerp, or rewrite it to take the already-swept eye. Pure helper in camera_math.js: `retailViewerStep(prevEye, idealEye, frac, sweepFn) -> {sought, eye}`. Escape flag `?camViewerStep=off` (default-on, `!== "off"`, row in docs/url-flags.md next to camStiffness); flag off must be byte-identical to today. Tests: node tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs, with a fake sweep that clamps at x = -1. (a) Frame 1 eye is never beyond the plane. (b) After the clamp releases, the eye moves only frac of the way out. (c) Pressed against the wall for 30 frames, the per-frame delta is < 1e-3. (d) frac = 1 gives sought == ideal. (e) The forward vector is identical with and without the clamp. Update the static assertions at :249 and :260 that pin `this._applyStiffness(dt, finalX` so they pin the new order: the guard precedes the sweep, and the sweep call follows the lerp. Also run node tests/test_c1_facing_camera.cjs.

title: Camera collision is a chain of 8 separate JS-to-wasm sweeps, not one retail viewer transit: terrain is clamped instead of swept, and scenery trees and rocks are never tested
decomp_evidence: SmartBox::update_viewer acclient.c:144991-145110 runs one CTransition. start_cell = player cell, or AdjustPosition(pivot) when indoor (:145054). init_object(player, 92) (:145086), init_sphere(1, &viewer_sphere, 1.0) (:145087), init_path(start_cell, pivot, sought), find_valid_position. On success, viewer = curr_pos and viewer_cell = curr_cell (:145091-145092). Otherwise AdjustPosition(sought). Otherwise viewer = player position with viewer_cell = 0. The transit collides with everything in the cells it crosses: landcell terrain polygons, building and EnvCell BSPs, and every shadow object. CPhysicsObj::FindObjCollisions :316159 exempts only creatures for a viewer (`if (transition->object_info.state & 4 && weenie->IsCreature()) return 1`). Scenery has no weenie, so it collides.
openac_evidence: PhysicsCameraCollisionProbe.cs:28-50: ResolveWithTransition(pivot to eye, sphere 0.3, IsViewer|PathClipped|FreeRotate|PerfectClip, skipping the self entity), then AdjustPosition(desiredEye), then (playerPos, 0). One call returns both eye and viewer cell. Tests: CameraCollisionIndoorTests.cs:28 SweepEye_OutdoorCell_StoppedByBuildingChannelShell, CameraCollisionUpdateViewerTests.cs:19 SweepEye_IndoorPivotInCellAboveFeet_SeatsStartAtPivotCell.
holt_evidence: camera.js:1509 `handle.terrainHeightAt(finalX, finalY)` raises finalZ at the end point only (:1511). Steps 2-6 (:1560-1690) each cross into wasm separately: cameraSweepCollision, sweepSphereAgainstBuildingMesh, sweepSphereAgainstStatics (:1581, LandblockInfo stab AABBs only), sweepSphereAgainstCellMesh, sweepSphereAgainstCellStatics, sweepSphereAgainstEntities (:1652), clipCameraToCellSpace (:1673). No camera step calls SpatialScene::sweep_sphere_against_scenery (scene.rs:4361); its only users are the player path and tests. cells.js:2170 then walks the same segment again with resolveViewerCell. scene.rs:5038 says: 'We have no camera transit'. The faithful driver already supports IS_VIEWER (holtburger-dat driver_validate.rs:415-417, objectinfo.rs:95-96) and is used for the player in faithful_bridge.rs:1738-1761.
discrepancy: (a) Procedural scenery has cylsphere physics that retail's camera collides with, but holtburger's camera passes through tree trunks and rocks. (b) Against slopes and ridges, holtburger lifts the eye vertically, which changes the view pitch, instead of pulling it in along the boom. A ridge between the pivot and the eye is never tested. (c) Two separate walks (clip chain at radius 0.5, viewer-cell walk at 0.3) can disagree about which cell the eye is in. (d) Up to 8 wasm crossings per frame plus a getRenderSet call.
proposed_change: Stage 1 (S): add a wasm export `sweepSphereAgainstScenery(from, to, radius, landblockId)` in lib.rs wrapping SpatialScene::sweep_sphere_against_scenery, and call it as step 4b in _clipCameraAgainstWorld. Stage 2 (L): add `SpatialScene::viewer_transit(player_cell, pivot, sought) -> (eye, cell)` in faithful_bridge.rs. Model it on the existing bridge: object_info.state = IS_VIEWER|PATH_CLIPPED|FREE_ROTATE|PERFECT_CLIP (0x5C); one sphere {center 0, r 0.3}; start cell by AdjustPosition(pivot) when indoor; init_path(start_cell, Some(pivot), sought); find_valid_position; then the two retail fallbacks; an object overlay that skips creatures and the player. Export it as `viewerTransit(...) -> Float32Array[x, y, z, cell]`. In camera.js, call it once in place of steps 1-6, keeping the old chain behind `?camTransit=off`. In cells.js updateViewerCell, take the transit's cell instead of calling resolveViewerCell.
test_plan: Rust #[test]s in crates/holtburger-world/src/spatial/tests.rs (orchestrator runs cargo test -p holtburger-world, capped). Reuse the scenery fixture near tests.rs:6102: viewer_transit_stops_at_scenery_cylsphere. Also: viewer_transit_terrain_ridge_pulls_in_along_boom (the eye ends on the pivot side of a ridge at the same heading, not raised), viewer_transit_crosses_portal_returns_neighbour_cell, and viewer_transit_invalid_start_falls_back_to_player_cell_zero. JS: a static assertion in tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs that _clipCameraAgainstWorld calls viewerTransit when the flag is on; run node apps/holtburger-web/tests/viewer_cell.test.mjs for the cells.js wiring.
already_tracked: no (scene.rs:5038 notes 'We have no camera transit' as a known gap; no open item)

verify.reasons: Decomp: SmartBox::update_viewer (acclient.c:144991-145110), re-read. Start cell is the player cell, or AdjustPosition(start_pos, &viewer_sphere) when (cell & 0xFFFF) >= 0x100. Then makeTransition, init_object(player, 92), init_sphere(1, &viewer_sphere, 1.0), init_path(start_cell, &begin_pos, &end_pos) and find_valid_position. On success it calls set_viewer(curr_pos) and sets viewer_cell = curr_cell; otherwise AdjustPosition(new_viewer); otherwise set_viewer(player m_position, 1) with viewer_cell = 0. CPhysicsObj::FindObjCollisions (:316159) returns early for a viewer only when `transition->object_info.state & 4 && weenie->vfptr[11]()` (IsCreature), so a weenie-less scenery object collides. Holtburger: _clipCameraAgainstWorld (camera.js:1475-1690). Step 1 is `handle.terrainHeightAt(finalX, finalY)` at the END point only (:1509-1511). Steps 2-6 are separate wasm calls, plus getRenderSet(1) and getLocalPlayerPose. sweepSphereAgainstStatics (lib.rs ~38461) queries only `statics_aabbs_near_pose` (scene.rs:4133), i.e. LandblockInfo stabs. Scenery colliders are a separate index, `scenery_colliders` (scene.rs:1302-1320), which by its own doc is distinct from statics on purpose. Its only users are `sweep_sphere_against_scenery` (scene.rs:4361) and its callers at :4472 and :4493 (the player path), plus tests (tests.rs:6102+). No camera export exists. title: Auto-follow does not follow in-place turns (turn-to-face on attack or cast, server turns, wasm pursuit turns)
decomp_evidence: CameraManager::UpdateCamera acclient.c:147425-147842 rebuilds pivot_frame from the player's frame every update (localtoglobalvec(player m_position, direction); viewer_offset is pivot-local, :147763), with no 'is moving' gate. Any heading change, including the server-driven TurnToHeading/TurnToObject, swings the camera at r_stiffness*dt*10 (0.45 means a rate of 4.5/s).
openac_evidence: RetailChaseCamera.cs: the heading is recomputed from playerYaw on every Update (ComputeHeading at the start of Update, `headingYaw = playerYaw + YawOffset`); the boom is then lerped with ComputeDampingAlpha(0.45, dt). There is no movement gate.
holt_evidence: camera.js:1110-1126 _isPlayerDriving() is true only if the XY position moved (`moved = dx*dx + dy*dy > ...`, :1119) or a WASDQE key is held (:1125). picking.js:857 turnToFaceThenAct turns via `sessionHandle.setMovementInput(0, 0, gate.turn, false)` with no key held and no translation; the same holds for loop.js server turns through turnToHeading. camera.js:244 AUTOFOLLOW_RATE_DEFAULT = 4.0.
discrepancy: When the character turns in place to face a target (melee or cast turn-to-face, a server TurnTo, a wasm pursuit turn), holtburger's camera stays where it was, so the player ends up facing sideways or toward the camera. In retail the camera swings around behind the character with the turn. The ease rate (4.0/s) is also slightly off retail's 10 x 0.45 = 4.5/s.
proposed_change: Track `_lastFollowHeading` in _isPlayerDriving. Return true when |wrapAngle(h - _lastFollowHeading)| > 1e-3 rad since the last frame, using the heading already read by _playerHeadingForFollow; pass it in to avoid a second pose read. This keeps the owner's 'idle holds the camera' behaviour for a truly idle character. Set AUTOFOLLOW_RATE_DEFAULT to 4.5 (and the Camera-tab default autoFollowRate in ui/camera_settings.js) to match retail stiffness 0.45. Extract the decision as a pure `followDrivingNow({moved, keyed, headingDelta})` in camera_math.js.
test_plan: node apps/holtburger-web/tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs. Pure cases: followDrivingNow({moved:false, keyed:false, headingDelta:0.3}) is true; headingDelta 5e-4 is false; a delta across +/-pi is wrapped. So in-place turns that are not keyed leave the camera put. AUTOFOLLOW_RATE_DEFAULT = 4.0 (:244), and camera_settings.js DEFAULTS autoFollowRate 4.0. verify.corrections: The proposed fix over-corrects relative to retail. Retail keeps the camera's PLAYER-RELATIVE offset: CameraSet::Rotate in third person rotates viewer_offset inside the pivot frame (:148788 non-in-head branch), so an in-place turn rotates the camera by the SAME heading delta and does not swing it to directly behind. Treating a heading change as 'driving' makes holtburger's autofollow ease followYaw all the way to behind the character. A user who has orbited to look at the character's front would get a 180 deg swing on a 10 deg cast face-turn. The 4.0 to 4.5 rate change is not a retail constant. Update `this._lastFollowHeading` EVERY frame before any early return, so a drag or grace period does not leave a stale reference that later fires a large delta. Then, when `this._autoFollowOn && this.mode === "follow" && !(this._retailZoomOn && this._inHead) && !this._followDragging`, the character is not driving (moved false and keyed false; split _isPlayerDriving so both booleans are available), and |wrapAngle(h - lastH)| > 1e-3: apply `this.followYaw += wrapAngle(h - lastH)` (rigid; the existing ease-to-behind still governs the driving case, so there is no double count). Add a static assertion that _updateAutoFollow calls inPlaceTurnYawDelta and writes _lastFollowHeading before its early returns. Leave AUTOFOLLOW_RATE_DEFAULT at 4.0.

title: No slope alignment: retail tilts the camera's heading frame to the contact plane (m_bAlignCameraToSlope, default on); holtburger's boom and look direction are always horizontal

CameraManager::UpdateCamera :147604-147700 runs `if (m_bAlignCameraToSlope && target_status & 0x10)`: it pushes the player velocity into a 5-entry ring (old_velocities) and averages it. If |avg.x| and |avg.y| >= 0.0002, the plane normal is the contact-plane normal when the player is in contact (state & 1), otherwise set_vector_heading((v.x, v.y, 0.1*v.z)). The player forward is projected onto that plane to give pivot_direction, so viewer_offset and the LOOK_IN_DIRECTION view pitch up when running uphill and down when running downhill.

proposed_change: Add velocity_x/y/z and contact_normal_x/y/z (plus in_contact) to LocalPlayerPose in lib.rs, filled from the integrator body's velocity and contact plane. In camera_math.js, port OpenAC ComputeHeading, PushVelocity/AverageVelocity (5-ring) and the alignment threshold as pure functions. title: Optimistic pickup/drop/wield sounds play at click time AND again when ACE's real 0xF750 arrives (300 ms echo window is shorter than ACE's move-to + pickup-animation delay)
decomp_evidence: Retail has no client-predicted inventory sounds. The only client callers of SoundManager::PlaySoundA are SmartBox::HandleSoundEvent (acclient.c:143333-143350) -> CPhysicsObj::play_sound (316424-316434) -> PlaySoundA(stype, obj, volume) (383655-383678), plus the hook Execute functions (SoundHook/SoundTweakedHook/SoundTableHook::Execute 342188-342221). So in retail the pickup/drop/wield sound plays only when the server's Sound message arrives, i.e. when the action actually happens. ACE cross-check (external/ACE Player_Inventory.cs): a ground pickup sends GameMessageSound(Guid, Sound.PickUpItem) only inside pickupChain.AddAction after the MoveTo + AddPickupChainToMoveToChain (line 1089). Drop runs StartPickupChain (640-658: EnqueueBroadcastMotion(Pickup); pickupChain.AddDelaySeconds(pickupAnimationLength)) and then sends Sound.DropItem (line 1445). Rejections send InventoryServerSaveFailed with no sound.
openac_evidence: OpenAC updates the item table optimistically (Core/Items/ClientObjectTable.cs:447 MoveItemOptimistic, :480 WieldItemOptimistic), but sound comes only from the server SoundEvent: App/Rendering/Vfx/EntityEffectController.cs:90-108 HandleSound -> PlayServerSound (336). No client-predicted cue.
holt_evidence: plugins/audio_optimistic.js:169 playOptimistic plays the player's SoundTable row at click time ({ gain: 1.0 } at :223) and records a suppression claim with `const TTL_MS = 300;` (:130). shouldSuppressEcho (:150-162) returns false once `now > expires` (:155), so a later echo plays. Call sites: plugins/item_drag.js:627 `if (!s?.owned) sfx(0x8F, guid);` (ground or chest pickup), :665 sfx(0x8C) wield, :683 sfx(0x90) drop; plugins/radial-menu.js:364/373 (0x8C), 391 (0x8D), 425/430/462 (0x90 drop / split-to-3D); plugins/inventory.js:763 (0x8D). Echo check: app/client_events.js:1995 `if (window.__audioOptimistic?.shouldSuppressEcho?.(sndEnum, sndGuid))`.
discrepancy: For any pickup from the ground or a container, any drop, and any wield that needs a move-to, ACE's sound arrives after the walk and the pickup animation, which is far longer than the 300 ms TTL. The player therefore hears the sound twice: once at the click, before walking and bending down, and once at the real moment. With round-trip latency over 300 ms, every inventory sound doubles. When the server rejects the action (too far, encumbered, already taken), the player hears a pickup/drop sound for something that never happened. Retail plays exactly one sound, in step with the server's action.
proposed_change: Stop predicting server-echoed sounds. In plugins/audio_optimistic.js add `const OPTIMISTIC_ON = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('audioOptimistic') === 'on'` (opt-in only, because retail parity is the default). In playOptimistic, return early when `!UI_SOUNDS.has(soundId) && !OPTIMISTIC_ON`, so 0x8C/0x8D/0x8E/0x8F/0x90 are left to the 0xF750 handler. The UI-only cues (0x6D UI_GeneralError, 0x73/0x74 slider) keep playing through playUiSound because the server never echoes them. Leave shouldSuppressEcho as is (with no claims recorded it always returns false). Optionally delete the sfx(...) calls in item_drag.js, radial-menu.js and inventory.js to make the intent explicit. Document the flag in docs/url-flags.md.
test_plan: Extend apps/holtburger-web/test_audio_optimistic.mjs (`node test_audio_optimistic.mjs` from apps/holtburger-web). (1) With the default location.search, playOptimistic(0x8F) and playOptimistic(0x90) make no audioManager.play call, and shouldSuppressEcho(0x8F, LPG) returns false right afterwards, so the server's 0xF750 plays exactly once. (2) playOptimistic(0x6D/0x73/0x74) still reaches playFromCenter. (3) With location.search='?audioOptimistic=on', the old behaviour (play plus a 300 ms claim) is unchanged. Before the fix, a scripted 'optimistic fire, then echo at +1200 ms' produces 2 plays; after it, 1.

title: Sounds on wielded (attached) items use the hand-local root.position, so a weapon/shield/wand buff 'landing' sound is placed near the world origin and culled (silent)
decomp_evidence: CPhysicsObj::set_parent (acclient.c:322952-) calls change_cell(child, parent->cell) and then CPhysicsObj::UpdateChild. UpdateChild (320039-320056) does Frame::combine(&new_frame, &parts[part_index]->pos.frame, child_frame) and set_frame(child_obj, &new_frame), so the child's m_position is a WORLD frame, and then runs ScriptManager::UpdateScripts(child_obj->script_manager). CPhysicsObj::play_script(PScriptType) (320326-) needs this->cell (set by set_parent) and queues the script on the child's own ScriptManager. Its SoundTableHook::Execute -> PlaySoundA(stype, physobj) (342219-342221, 383681-383703) plays at &physobj->m_position using the child's own sound_table. ACE WorldObject_Magic.cs:361-365 DoSpellEffects broadcasts GameMessageScript(target.Guid, spell.TargetEffect) with target = the wielded item. DAT check (portal.dat, my python btree reader): the weapon PhysicsScriptTable 0x3400002B, used by every melee/missile/caster weenie in LSD, has 16 of 17 first scripts containing a SoundTable(2) hook at t=0 (e.g. key 0x39 -> 0x330000EE hooks [13,2,13]).
openac_evidence: OpenAC places script and server sounds at the owner's ROOT WORLD pose: App/Rendering/Vfx/EntityEffectController.cs:336-344 PlaySoundServerSound uses `_poses.TryGetRootPose(ownerLocalId, out Matrix4x4 rootWorld) ? rootWorld.Translation : Vector3.Zero`, and :541-544 refreshes PhysicsScriptRunner owner anchors the same way (Core/Vfx/PhysicsScriptRunner.cs:56 SetOwnerAnchor, :269 dispatch uses the anchor).
holt_evidence: Attach reparents the child under the wielder's part: scene3d/entities.js:6698 `mount.add(c.root);` and :6717 `c.root.position.set(loc.ox, loc.oy, loc.oz);`, so root.position becomes a hand-local offset. Every sound site still reads the raw root.position as if it were global AC metres: _fireHook (16374) `const pos = inst.root.position;` (16416) -> Sound(1) `acToThree(pos.x,pos.y,pos.z)` (16451); SoundTable(2) `const px = inst.root.position.x;` (16533); SoundTweaked(21) `acToThree(pos.x, pos.y, pos.z)` (16772); _firePlayEffectSoundHook (13683) `const pos = rig?.position ?? {x:0,y:0,z:0};` (13706); app/client_events.js:1950 `const pos = inst.root?.position;` (0xF750); follow-mode lookup in scene3d/index.js:2500 `const p = inst?.root?.position;`. Wire PlayEffect sounds reach the child through play_effect_vfx.js:2453 `em._firePlayEffectSoundHook(targetGuid >>> 0, desc)`. In audio_manager.js _playHrtf, retailAttenuation(dist ~ tens of km) gives play:false, so the sound is skipped.
discrepancy: Retail plays a wielded item's script and sound hooks (item-enchant TargetEffect chimes, SoundTable hooks, server sounds on the item guid) at the item's world position, i.e. at the player's hand. Holtburger places them at the hand-local offset (about (0.05, 0, 0.1)), interpreted as global coordinates, which is near (0,0,0) and thousands of metres from the listener. They are culled at -50 dB and never heard. The follow-mode panner update has the same bug.
proposed_change: Add a pure helper module scene3d/audio/emitter_position.js: `export function emitterPosThree(inst, scratchV3)`. It returns null without inst.root. When `inst._attachedParentGuid != null` (or `inst.root.userData.__attachedChildOf`), it returns `inst.root.getWorldPosition(scratchV3)` copied to {x,y,z}; this is already in the three.js listener frame because worldRoot's -pi/2 rotation and the hand part transform are both included. Otherwise it returns acToThree(root.position). Use it instead of `acToThree(inst.root.position...)` in entities.js _fireHook (Sound 1, SoundTable 2 at resolve time, SoundTweaked 21), _firePlayEffectSoundHook (ht 1/21; ht 2 goes through _fireHook), the legacy ?scriptQueue=off walker arm (rig.position), app/client_events.js runServerSound, and the scene3d/index.js updateFollowingPositions lookup. Keep the AC-frame world_pos in event-log records by converting back with threeToAc from retail_mixer.js. Related render issue, not part of this audio fix: play_effect_vfx.js:797-818 _resolveTargetPlacement uses inst.root.position too, so placeholder bursts on wielded items land at the origin.
test_plan: New tests/audio_attached_emitter.test.mjs (`node tests/audio_attached_emitter.test.mjs`; three.js is already imported by tests such as tests/projectile_spin.test.mjs). Build worldRoot (rotation.x=-PI/2) -> entitiesGroup -> parent root at AC (32450, 28010, 60) -> part node at (0,0,1.2) -> child root at local (0.05,0,0.1) with inst._attachedParentGuid set. Assert emitterPosThree(child) is within 0.5 m of acToThree(32450.05, 28010, 61.3). Assert emitterPosThree(topLevel) equals acToThree(root.position) exactly, so non-attached entities are unchanged. Assert retail_mixer getAttenuation(distance(listener at the parent, helper result), 1, 1).play === true, while the old raw-local path gives play === false.

verify.reasons: Decomp: CPhysicsObj::set_parent(obj, part_index, frame) (acclient.c:323003-323027) calls change_cell(child, parent->cell) and then UpdateChild. UpdateChild (320039-320056) does `Frame::combine(&new_frame, &parts[part_index]->pos.frame, child_frame); set_frame(child_obj, &new_frame)`, then UpdateScripts. The child's m_position is therefore a world frame at the hand. SoundTableHook / SoundHook / SoundTweakedHook::Execute (342188-342221) call PlaySoundA(..., physobj), which plays at `&physobj->m_position` (383481, 383508, 383697). ACE WorldObject_Magic.cs:356-366 DoSpellEffects: `targetBroadcaster = target.Wielder ?? target; targetBroadcaster.EnqueueBroadcast(new GameMessageScript(target.Guid, spell.TargetEffect, ...))`, so item-enchant effects address the wielded item's guid. LSD check: Long Sword 351, Buckler 44 and Wand 2472 all carry SoundTable (did 3) = 0x20000014 and PhysicsEffectTable (did 22) = 0x3400002B, so wielded items do own sound and script tables. Holtburger: entities.js attachChildToParent does `mount.add(c.root)` (6717) and `c.root.position.set(loc.ox, loc.oy, loc.oz)` (6736). Entities otherwise sit at global AC metres (`lbX * 192 + meta.x`, 4972). Every sound site still reads the raw root.position: _fireHook `const pos = inst.root.position` (16443) -> `acToThree(pos.x,pos.y,pos.z)` for Sound(1); SoundTable(2) `const px = inst.root.position.x` (16560); the SoundTweaked(21) `twkT` (~16800); _firePlayEffectSoundHook `const pos = rig?.position ?? ...` (13733); the legacy walker `rig.position` (~13848); client_events runServerSound `inst.root?.position` (1968) -> acToThree (2027); index.js updateFollowingPositions `inst?.root?.position` (2500). play_effect_vfx.js:2453 `em._firePlayEffectSoundHook(targetGuid >>> 0, desc)` does not redirect to the wielder. audio_manager._playHrtf (777-795) computes the distance to the listener (camera, three frame), and retail_mixer.getAttenuation (51-61) returns play:false below -50 dB, so a hand-local (~0,0,0) emitter thousands of metres from the listener is skipped. The bug is verified mechanically for any sound addressed to an attached child.
verify.corrections: Line drift: _fireHook is at 16401 (pos at 16443, SoundTable px at 16560), _firePlayEffectSoundHook at 13710/13733, client_events at 1968/2027 (not 1950), and index.js 2500 is correct. I could not verify the DAT claim that 16 of 17 scripts in 0x3400002B carry a t=0 SoundTable hook (no DAT parse in this read-only phase), so the size of the audible impact is unquantified. The positioning bug itself is certain. getWorldPosition is in the three.js world frame, which is the listener's frame because worldRoot only carries rotation.x = -PI/2 (index.js:1503-1505, no translation) and the listener is camera.position. The helper therefore matches acToThree for top-level rigs. Keep the non-attached path as acToThree(root.position) so nothing else changes.
verify.implementation_notes: New pure module scene3d/audio/emitter_position.js. Do not import THREE or adapter.js; inline acToThree as `[x, z, -y]`, the way audio_optimistic.js does. Export `emitterPosThree(inst, scratch)`: return null if `!inst?.root`. If `inst._attachedParentGuid != null && inst.root.parent && typeof inst.root.getWorldPosition === 'function'`, call `inst.root.getWorldPosition(scratch)` (which updates the ancestor matrices) and return `{x: scratch.x, y: scratch.y, z: scratch.z}`. Otherwise return `{x: p.x, y: p.z, z: -p.y}` from root.position. Also export `emitterPosAc(inst, scratch)` = threeToAc(emitterPosThree(...)) (threeToAc is in retail_mixer.js:135), so event-log world_pos stays in the AC frame. Fallback when the attached child's root has no parent (mid re-park): use the wielder's root from `entityMap.get(inst._attachedParentGuid)`, or skip. Replace these sites: entities.js _fireHook Sound(1) (pos and sndT), SoundTable(2) (px/py/pz and stbT; resolve the position at play time), SoundTweaked(21) (twkT); _firePlayEffectSoundHook ht 1/21 (look up `this.entityMap.get(guid)` at fire time, use the helper, and tighten `entityMap.has` to an identity check `=== inst`); the legacy ?scriptQueue=off walker arm (~13848); app/client_events.js runServerSound (1968/2027); scene3d/index.js updateFollowingPositions lookup (2500). Use a module-level THREE.Vector3 scratch in entities.js and index.js. Escape flag: `?attachedSoundPos=off` restores the raw-local read; document it in url-flags.md. Do NOT touch play_effect_vfx.js _resolveTargetPlacement (797-818): it has the same bug for particles, but that is a render change (separate, visual_impact=render). Test: new tests/audio_attached_emitter.test.mjs (`import * as THREE from 'three'`, as tests/projectile_spin.test.mjs does). Build worldRoot (rotation.x=-PI/2) -> group -> parent root at AC (32450,28010,60) -> part node at (0,0,1.2) -> child root at local (0.05,0,0.1) with `_attachedParentGuid` set. Assert emitterPosThree(child) is within 0.5 of acToThree(32450.05,28010,61.3), that a top-level inst's result equals acToThree(root.position) exactly, and that getAttenuation(dist(listener at the parent, helper), 1, 1).play === true while the raw-local path gives false. Register it in harness/run-js-headless.mjs (tier 5, like the audio_* entries at ~355-357).

title: Pre-create queues are split: PlayScripts (and the sound hooks inside them) expire 3 s per entry, server sounds 25 s sliding, attach/visibility in a third buffer, and drain order is by kind rather than arrival
decomp_evidence: SmartBox::HandleSoundEvent (acclient.c:143333-143350), HandlePlayScriptID (143354-143372) and HandlePlayScriptType (143375-143393) all call CObjectMaint::QueueBlobForObject for an unknown guid. QueueBlobForObject (310848-310861) puts every blob kind on ONE null object (GetNullObject(id,1)) via CPhysicsObj::queue_netblob (a single FIFO). AddObjectToBeDestroyed (310650-310672) re-arms that one null object's destruction at cur_time + 25.0 on every queued blob. When the object is created, the blobs replay in arrival order.
openac_evidence: App/Rendering/Vfx/EntityEffectController.cs:105/108 (Sound) and :128 (Typed PlayScript) both call one `Enqueue(serverGuid, PendingEffect)` (a single Queue<PendingEffect> per guid, ~547-555). TryReplayPending (558-568) replays the whole queue FIFO through Execute (Direct / Typed / Sound).
holt_evidence: PlayEffects for unknown guids use their own queue with `const _PENDING_TTL_MS = 3000;` per entry (scene3d/play_effect_vfx.js:3199, pruned per entry at 3245), capped at 8 per guid and 256 guids. Server sounds use PendingObjectSounds with a 25 s sliding deadline (scene3d/audio/retail_sound_rules.js OBJECT_BLOB_TTL_S). Attach and visibility use the generic `this._preCreate` buffer (scene3d/pre_create_buffer.js, 25 s sliding). On spawn the drains run in fixed kind order: entities.js:5242 drainPendingPlayEffects, :5244 drainPendingObjectSounds, then :5331 this._drainPreCreate(guid). So a wielded child's queued effect or sound replays before its parked attach is applied.
discrepancy: In retail, a PlayScript that arrives 4-25 s before its object (or that is kept alive by a later sound or effect blob) still plays, including its sound hooks, and all blobs replay in arrival order. Holtburger drops script effects and their sounds after 3 s even while a later sound keeps the guid alive. It also replays PlayEffects and sounds before a parked ParentEvent, so effects on a just-created wielded item play at its pre-attach pose.
proposed_change: Route both kinds into the generic buffer that already has retail semantics. In play_effect_vfx.js, at the missing-target enqueue site, call `em._preCreate.enqueue(guid, 'playEffect', {scriptId, speed, silent, ...})` when `em._preCreateBufferOn`. In app/client_events.js runServerSound's !inst branch, call `emgr._preCreate.enqueue(sndGuid, 'sound', {replay})` instead of pendingObjectSounds.add. In entities.js _drainPreCreate, handle 'playEffect' (call the existing replay function used by drainPendingPlayEffects) and 'sound' (call replay()) in FIFO order alongside attach/visibility. Move the drainPendingPlayEffects/drainPendingObjectSounds calls at 5242-5244 into the ?preCreateBuffer=off arm only. Keep the old queues as the off-path.
test_plan: Extend the existing pure test for scene3d/pre_create_buffer.js, or add tests/pre_create_mixed_kinds.test.mjs using createPreCreateBuffer({now}): enqueue playEffect at t=0, sound at t=20 s, attach at t=21 s; at t=30 s takeFor(guid) returns all three in arrival order; at t=46.001 s the bucket has expired. Add an arm to tests/audio_server_sound.test.mjs asserting that a 0xF750 for an unknown guid goes into the generic buffer and replays once on drain.
already_tracked: partly: the PARITY-STATUS audio open item about the 25 s sliding deadline was fixed for server sounds only (3133629c); the 3 s PlayEffect TTL and the cross-kind order are not tracked

verify.reasons: Confirmed facts: play_effect_vfx.js:3199 `const _PENDING_TTL_MS = 3000;` with per-entry pruning in _pruneExpired (3239-3262), plus caps of 8 per guid and 256 guids (3197-3198). retail_sound_rules.js:128 OBJECT_BLOB_TTL_S = 25.0 with a sliding deadline (154, fixed in 3133629c). pre_create_buffer.js is a 25 s sliding FIFO for attach / visibility only. In the spawn path, entities.js:5261 drainPendingPlayEffects and :5263 drainPendingObjectSounds run before :5350 _drainPreCreate. Retail: SmartBox::HandleSoundEvent (143333), HandlePlayScriptID (143354) and HandlePlayScriptType (143375) all call QueueBlobForObject (310848-310861). That puts every blob on one null object via queue_netblob (an NIList FIFO append, 144770-144810, replayed head-first at ~145787), and AddObjectToBeDestroyed (310651-310672) re-arms cur_time + 25.0 on every blob. A PlayScript that arrives 3-25 s before its object is therefore dropped by holtburger but replayed by retail, and a later sound does not keep the effects alive. Refuted or incomplete: the ordering argument. In retail the parent link of a wielded item is usually NOT a queued blob. It is applied at object creation, from the wielder's PhysicsDesc children list (CObjectMaint::SetChildren 310888-310930 -> set_parent, which even parents an unknown child's null object) or from the child's own PhysicsDesc, BEFORE the queued blobs replay. Only a wire ParentEvent for an unknown object is queued in the same FIFO (SmartBox::HandleParentEvent 144512-144545). So a pure arrival-order FIFO merge would still replay pre-create PlayEffects BEFORE a create-time attach, which is the opposite of retail. And attachChildToParent is async (it awaits _resolveHoldingLocation, ~6675-6690), so no queue ordering can make a replayed effect see the mounted pose synchronously. With audio-2 unfixed, the post-attach position is wrong anyway.
verify.corrections: The cross-kind 'arrival order' fix does not achieve the stated goal for create-time attaches; retail applies create-time parenting before the netblob replay. The generic buffer has no per-guid or max-guid caps, so moving PlayEffects into it drops the existing 8/256 bounds (retail has none, but this is a robustness change that should be stated). The existing comment in entities.js attributing create-time set_parent to acclient.c:330260 is wrong: 330260 is ParticleEmitter::SetParenting. The real create-time paths are CObjectMaint::SetChildren (310928) and the child's PhysicsDesc. Severity LOW is right: ACE only broadcasts to clients that already know the object, so the 3-25 s window is rare.
verify.implementation_notes: Do not implement the FIFO merge as proposed. Separately safe narrow follow-up, if wanted: in play_effect_vfx.js replace the per-entry `_PENDING_TTL_MS = 3000` prune with a per-guid sliding deadline (bucket.lastQueuedAt re-armed on every _enqueuePlayEffect; expire the whole bucket at lastQueuedAt + 25000), mirroring PendingObjectSounds (3133629c). Keep the 8/256 caps. Optionally let pendingObjectSounds.add() and _enqueuePlayEffect() share one 'touch(guid)' clock, so a sound keeps queued effects alive and vice versa. Test: extend the existing PlayEffect queue test (find it with `rg -l drainPendingPlayEffects tests/`) using an injected clock: enqueue at t=0, again at t=20 s, drain at t=30 s and expect both to replay; drain at t=45.001 s and expect none. Ordering design for later: at spawn commit, apply the create-time attach first, and defer replaying the effects and sounds for that guid until attachChildToParent's promise settles (an await or a .then chain), only when the guid has a parked attach.

title: Wire PlayScripts (and their sound hooks) are not serialized on the owner's ScriptManager, so back-to-back scripts on one object overlap instead of queueing
decomp_evidence: CPhysicsObj::play_script(PScriptType) (acclient.c:320326-) -> play_script_internal -> ScriptManager::AddScript -> AddScriptInternal (329069-): `if (last_data) start = last_data->script->length + last_data->start_time; else start = cur_time`. ScriptManager::UpdateScripts (329189-) / NextHook fire hooks at script.start_time + hook.start_time and move on to the next script only after the current one finishes. CallPES with a pause uses an FPHook and then the same play_script_internal path (318973-319005).
openac_evidence: Core/Vfx/PhysicsScriptRunner.cs:90-92 `double start = owner.Scripts.Count == 0 ? _clock() : owner.Scripts[^1].StartTime + owner.Scripts[^1].Duration;`. Direct and typed wire PlayScripts both go through PlayDirect (63) / Play (129).
holt_evidence: Entity-spawn and CallPES scripts use the owner queue (entities.js _queuePhysicsScript ~14071, default-on ?scriptQueue). The wire PlayEffect path does not: play_effect_vfx.js:2423-2453 decodes the script's Sound/SoundTable/SoundTweaked hooks and calls em._firePlayEffectSoundHook immediately; that function (entities.js:13683) schedules each one with setTimeout(startTime) from receipt, with no reference to the owner's ScriptManager.
discrepancy: In retail, a second PlayScript on the same object (rapid buff casts on one target, several debuffs landing together, a hit effect on a creature running a looping default script) starts after the earlier script's length, so its sound follows the first one. Holtburger starts every wire script at receipt, so the cues overlap and stack. This also bypasses the despawn cleanup that the owner's ScriptManager gets.
proposed_change: In play_effect_vfx.js, after resolving the PES entries for a live target and once the dedup/synthetic-caster bookkeeping is done, hand the entries to `em._queuePhysicsScript(targetGuid, inst.root, pesId, entries)` when SCRIPT_QUEUE_ON, instead of firing sound hooks directly through _firePlayEffectSoundHook. Particle hooks would then also go through _executeScriptHook. Keep the soundOnly / silent dedup modes by filtering entries before queueing. Behaviour change for VFX timing too, so coordinate with the particles_vfx facet owner.
test_plan: Add an arm to apps/holtburger-web/tests/test_ws09_play_effect_sound.mjs (or the existing script-queue test): two wire PlayEffects on the same guid, 50 ms apart, with a fake script of length 1.0 s containing a t=0 SoundTable hook. Assert the second sound fires at ~1.0 s after the first (fake clock), not at +50 ms. Assert a despawn between them cancels the second sound.

verify.reasons: Decomp: CPhysicsObj::play_script_internal (318035-318063) creates the ScriptManager and calls ScriptManager::AddScript (329124) -> AddScriptInternal (329069-329121): `if (last_data) start = last_data->script->length + last_data->start_time; else start = cur_time`. UpdateScripts (329189-329233) and NextHook (329142-329187) advance to the next script only after the current one's hooks are exhausted. OpenAC PhysicsScriptRunner.cs:90-92 chains the same way (`owner.Scripts[^1].StartTime + owner.Scripts[^1].Duration`). Holtburger: entities.js _queuePhysicsScript (14401) is the serialized owner queue (SCRIPT_QUEUE_ON default on, 2057-2067), but play_effect_vfx.js never calls it (rg finds no `_queuePhysicsScript` in that file). The wire path's sound hooks go to em._firePlayEffectSoundHook (2453), which runs a raw setTimeout(startTime) from receipt (entities.js 13710-13752). Particles are spawned by play_effect_vfx's own resolver. Two wire scripts on one owner therefore overlap instead of chaining.
verify.corrections: 'Bypasses the despawn cleanup' is overstated: _firePlayEffectSoundHook already drops a fire when `!this.entityMap.has(guid)` at fire time (13730, 13748). The real gap is only a same-guid respawn, because it checks `has`, not identity. The proposed fix (hand the wire entries to _queuePhysicsScript) moves particle hooks onto a different spawner: entities _fireHook 13/26 anchors on rig part frames, while play_effect_vfx anchors placements under entitiesGroup (1361, 797-818). It also bypasses play_effect_vfx's dedup / castVfx / HIDEFX lifecycle logic. That changes what is drawn and where, so visual_impact is render rather than behaviour. Moving only the sound hooks into the owner queue would desync them from the particles and give wrong script lengths. Effort L.
verify.implementation_notes: Defer to the particles_vfx facet. A correct design keeps play_effect_vfx's particle spawner but schedules the whole wire script (particles and sounds) at the owner ScriptManager's chained start time. For example, ask the owner's ScriptManager for `nextStartTime(guid)` (last.startTime + last.length, or now if empty), register a placeholder script of the same length so later scripts chain behind it, and offset every hook's setTimeout by (start - now). Flag it as `?wireScriptQueue` (default ON with an `=off` escape, per the PARITY-STATUS flag policy). Test: tests/test_ws09_play_effect_sound.mjs or the script_manager test, with a fake clock: two wire PlayEffects on one guid 50 ms apart, script length 1.0 s, t=0 SoundTable hook; the second sound should fire at about +1.0 s. title: SoundTableCache.resolveSound crosses the wasm boundary and allocates/frees N SoundEntryJs handles on every play (footsteps, server sounds, UI clicks)
decomp_evidence: Retail SoundManager::GetSound (acclient.c:383433-383463) is a hash lookup into the resident CSoundTable (CSoundTable::Lookup 385195 -> SoundTableData::Lookup) that copies 4 fields into a stack SoundData. There is no per-play allocation.
openac_evidence: Core/Audio/SoundCookbook.cs:42-47 Select(table, sound, rng) indexes the already-parsed table.Sounds[sound].Entries list directly; PickVariant (11-23) allocates nothing.
holt_evidence: scene3d/audio/sound_table_cache.js:212 resolveSound calls `entries = stb.entriesForSound(enumU32);` (219) on every call, snapshots one entry, then frees every wasm handle (`e.free()`, 262). The wasm side, apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs:46094-46100 entries_for_sound, does `Some(v) => v.clone()`, i.e. a fresh Vec<SoundEntryJs> and N wasm-bindgen wrapper objects each time.
discrepancy: Every sound event pays a wasm call, N wrapper allocations and N frees (each going through FinalizationRegistry bookkeeping) for data that never changes. With many walking creatures this means hundreds of allocations per second on the main thread for nothing.
proposed_change: Memoize plain rows per (did, soundEnum) in SoundTableCache. Add `this._rows = new Map()` keyed by `did * 0x10000 + enum` (or a nested Map) holding a frozen array of {waveDid, priority, probability, volume} POJOs, built once from entriesForSound and the handles freed right away. resolveSound then does the same uniform `Math.floor((rows.length-1) * this._rng())` pick on the cached array and returns the POJO, or a shallow copy if callers mutate it. Clear _rows in dispose(). Note: the JSDoc at lib.rs:46091-46093 still describes the old 'probability-weighted' pick; fix that comment when lib.rs is next touched (no rebuild needed for this change).
test_plan: New tests/audio_sound_table_cache.test.mjs (there is currently no test for this module). Use a fake fetchSoundTable whose entriesForSound counts calls and returns objects with free(). (1) 100 resolveSound(did, 0x37) calls invoke entriesForSound once. (2) The pick is uniform floor((N-1)*r): with N=2, r=0.999 still returns entry 0 (retail quirk, OpenAC SoundCookbookTests PickVariant_TwoEntries_LastIsUnreachable); with N=3, r=0.5 returns entry 1. (3) Every handle's free() was called exactly once. (4) dispose() clears the row cache.

verify.reasons: scene3d/audio/sound_table_cache.js: resolveSound (212) calls `stb.entriesForSound(enumU32)` (219) on every call, reads 4 getters from the picked handle, and frees every handle (`e.free()`, 262). The wasm side, src/lib.rs:46405-46410 `entries_for_sound`, returns `match self.sounds.get(&sound_enum) { Some(v) => v.clone(), None => Vec::new() }`, so each play allocates a fresh Vec and N wasm-bindgen wrappers plus FinalizationRegistry bookkeeping, and each getter is another boundary crossing. Retail SoundManager::GetSound (acclient.c:383433-383463) does a CSoundTable::Lookup and copies 4 fields into a stack SoundData, with no allocation. OpenAC SoundCookbook.cs:11-47 indexes the parsed `table.Sounds[sound].Entries` directly. No existing test covers sound_table_cache.js. The returned entry is never mutated by any of the 12 resolveSound callers (rg for `entry.(waveDid|volume|probability|priority) =` found nothing).
verify.corrections: The lib.rs line is 46405, not 46094. The stale 'probability-weighted' JSDoc is at about 46398-46403; fix it whenever lib.rs is next touched, no rebuild needed for this change. 'Hundreds of allocations per second' is plausible but unmeasured. This is a LOW perf cleanup.
verify.implementation_notes: In SoundTableCache, add `this._rows = new Map()` in the constructor: Map<did, Map<enumU32, ReadonlyArray<{waveDid,priority,probability,volume}>>>. Use a nested Map, not `did*0x10000+enum`, so a large enum cannot collide. In resolveSound, after `const stb = await this.get(did)`, look up the rows. On a miss, call entriesForSound once, snapshot every entry into frozen POJOs, free all the handles (keep the existing try/catch and warn), and cache the array. Also cache an empty array for enums the table lacks, so a missing enum costs no wasm call. Keep the pick logic exactly as it is: 0 entries -> null; 1 entry -> rows[0] WITHOUT consuming this._rng (seeded tests and the entities.js probability roll read cache._rng afterwards); N entries -> `Math.floor((N-1) * this._rng())` clamped. title: Sky time of day and DayGroup run on a private 1999-anchored wall clock instead of the server PortalYearTicks clock (retail Timer::cur_time); 780 s ahead and on a different day than retail and the client's own map panel
decomp_evidence: GameTime::UseTime (acclient.c:463395-463416): `time = Timer::cur_time + this->clock_offset + this->time_zero_start_delta`; clock_offset is only ever zeroed (463386, 463475) and time_zero_start_delta = GameSky::s_timeAdjustment, a debug knob (308547). GameTime::CalcDayBegin (463203-463240): `total_time = time + zero_time_of_year; current_year = zero_year + floor(total/year_length); current_day = floor(offset_in_year/day_length)`. present_time_of_day = (time - time_of_day_begin)/day_length. Timer::cur_time IS the server clock: ClientNet::HandleTimeSynch (371516-371533) calls `Timer::set_time(&srvtime)`, and Timer::set_time (75365-75407) writes `Timer::cur_time = m_tExternalTime = srvtime`. SkyDesc::CalcPresentDayGroup (301664-301690) hashes `current_day + days_per_year*current_year` from GameTime, so the weather of the day is a pure function of server time. Server side: ACE sends Timers.PortalYearTicks in TimeSync and ConnectRequest (NetworkSession.cs:938, AuthenticationHandler.cs:119). That value starts at DerethDateTime.UtcNowToEMUTime = (UtcNow-5h) - 2017-01-31 12:00 (DerethDateTime.cs:1062), then accumulates per loop (WorldManager.cs:391), so it can drift from wall time.
openac_evidence: SkyState.cs:232-264: WorldTimeService.SyncFromServer(serverTicks) stores the ticks, and NowTicks = _lastSyncedTicks + elapsed*TickSize. DayFraction is Calendar.DayFraction(NowTicks). WorldSession.cs:1186-1192 raises TimeSync as ServerTimeUpdated, and WorldSession.Connection.cs:144-145 seeds it from the ConnectRequest time. RuntimeWorldEnvironmentState.cs:176 installs the Region origin (`WorldTime.Calendar.SetOriginOffset(definition.OriginOffsetTicks)`). Its :195-200 SynchronizeFromServer calls RefreshDayGroup, which picks the group from server ticks (:240-270). DerethDateTimeTests.cs:91-98 pins origin 3600: tick 291,408,060 is Seedsow 24, 116 P.Y.
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-world/src/sky.rs:62 `pub const AC_LAUNCH_UNIX_EPOCH: f64 = 941_500_800.0;`. :366 Default is `Self::new_with_anchor_unix(AC_LAUNCH_UNIX_EPOCH)`. :432-434 `(now_unix - self.anchor_unix) + game_time.zero_time_of_year`. :572-574 game_time_dpy hardcodes `360` instead of GameTime.days_per_year. apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs:20122 `let now_unix = js_date_now_ms() / 1000.0;` feeds evaluate(); :19704 builds `SkyEvalState::new()` with no server clock. src/session/messages/mod.rs:91-97 sends TimeSync only to WorldState::set_server_time_sync, never to the sky. scene3d/atmosphere_sky.js:46 and :64-69 apply the same 1999 anchor to the moon and stars. discrepancy: holtburger computes world seconds as now-941500800+3600, while retail and ACE use PortalYearTicks+3600 with PortalYearTicks ≈ now-1485882000. The two differ by 544,381,200 s, which is ≡ 780 s (mod 7620). So the holtburger sky is 780 s, or 0.102 of a day (about 1.6 of the 16 named hours), ahead of retail. The calendar day is also completely different. On 2026-10-08 holtburger is in year 319, day 305, while the server is in year 121 P.Y., day 144. Different (day, year) seeds give a different DayGroup (Sunny/Rainy) than every retail client on the same server. The client's own map panel can say 'Time: Foredawn' while its sky shows Dawnsong. title: Command input misses retail prefixes and aliases: '@' bypasses client verbs, ':'/';' emote shortcuts, verb aliases, inline *pose* tokens, and %p gender
decomp_evidence: ClientCommunicationSystem::OnChatCommand (acclient.c:426126): `case 47: SetAtIndex(0, 64); return DoCommand` ('/' becomes '@'); `case 64: return DoCommand`; `case 58/59` (':' and ';') builds "@emote" + rest, then DoCommand. DoCommand (423537) does a case-insensitive hash lookup with the trailing comma trimmed; on a miss it tries DoChannelCommand, and only then sends Event_Talk(line). InitializeCommands (426432): e/em/emote/me map to DoEmote; c/covassal/covassals/co-vassals, f/fellow/fellows/fellowship/g/group/party, m/monarch, p/patron and v/vassal/vassals map to DoStupidChannelHack. PublicChat (426025) loops RemoveTextBetween('*','*') then ('<','>'), passing each token to Pose(); the token is removed only when Pose resolves a motion, and the remaining text is sent with Event_Talk only if non-empty. Pose (425512) replaces `%p` in otherEmote with "his" when PropertyInt 0x71 (Gender)==1, otherwise "her". HelpEmoteList (418786): "These commands should be bound on either side by asterisks. (Example: *wave*)".
openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Runtime/Chat/ChatInputParser.cs:100-115 reparses a known '@' verb as '/' and passes unknown @ lines through intact (pinned by tests/AcDream.UI.Abstractions.Tests/Panels/Chat/ChatInputParserAtPrefixTests.cs). ChatCommandRouter.cs:90-93 `if (trimmed[0] is ':' or ';') trimmed = "@emote " + trimmed[1..]`. RetailClientCommandCatalog.cs:474-477 maps e/em/emote/me to Emote. RetailPublicChatParser.ExtractPoses is used by LiveChatCommandRoute.RoutePublicChat (~213-228) and pinned by RetailPublicChatParserTests ("a *one* b <two> c" -> "a  b  c"). ChatPoseCatalog.cs:106-117 replaces %p with his/her by gender.
holt_evidence: app/slash_commands.js:76 `if (message.startsWith("@")) return { dispatched: false };`, so `@tell Bob, hi`, `@r`, `@f` and `@e` reach ACE Talk and come back as "Unknown command: tell" (ACE has no such CommandHandler). Line 211 handles only `me` for emotes, so `/e waves` falls through to `@e waves` at :362. CHANNEL_MAP (:155-164) has no c/covassal(s)/fellow(s)/fellowship/g/group/party/monarch/patron/vassal(s). A `:waves` line is spoken as text. chat_log.js buildOutgoingLine only lets '/' and '@' bypass the talk focus. index.html:4819-4851 sends plain speech unchanged, so `*wave*` is spoken and no animation plays. lib.rs resolve_soul_emote: `text.replace("%p", "their")`.
discrepancy: Commands in retail's '@' style (still the in-game help wording) and the ':'/';' emote shortcuts don't work. Several retail aliases are missing. The retail way to soul-emote (`*wave*`, including inline, e.g. 'hi *wave*') is spoken as literal text. Other players see 'their' where retail would say 'his' or 'her'.
proposed_change: In routeSlashCommand: normalise the first character so '@' behaves like '/' and ':'/';' becomes `/emote ` + rest. Match verbs case-insensitively with the trailing ',' trimmed. Add EMOTE_ALIASES {e,em,emote,me} and the retail channel aliases (alongside chat-1). Unknown verbs keep sending `@cmd rest` as today. Add an exported pure `extractPoses(text, resolve, execute)` that scans '*...*' then '<...>', strips a token only when handle.resolveSoulEmote(token)?.motionFull !== 0, and runs the existing soul-emote branch for it (sendSoulEmote, broadcastEmoteMotion, local prediction, 'You ...' echo). Call it on the plain-speech fall-through in index.html and send the remainder with sendChat only if non-empty. chat_log.js buildOutgoingLine: also pass ':'/';' lines through verbatim. These cases mirror OpenAC's RetailPublicChatParserTests. The %p part needs a Rust #[test] on a pure helper `possessive_for_gender(1)=='his'`, run by the orchestrator. verify.reasons: slash_commands.js:76 has `if (message.startsWith('@')) return { dispatched:false }`, so @tell, @r, @f and @e go to ACE Talk. None of tell/t/send/whisper/w/reply/r/rp/retell/rt/say/s/a/ab/f/fellow/g/group/party/c/m/p/v/cg/general/ct/trade/clfg/lfg/crp/roleplay/society/soc/olthoi/o/me/e/em/emote is an ACE CommandHandler (scanned ~/ace-server Command/Handlers, 323 names), so ACE reports them as unknown. Only 'me' is handled as /me (:211). CHANNEL_MAP (:155-164) lacks the retail channel aliases. chat_log.js buildOutgoingLine passes through only '/' and '@'. No ':', ';', '*...*' or '<...>' handling exists anywhere in apps/holtburger-web (rg). lib.rs resolve_soul_emote (~36983) does text.replace('%p','their') on both strings. Decomp: OnChatCommand (acclient.c:426126) handles case 47 '/' -> '@' -> DoCommand; case 64 -> DoCommand; case 58/59 rewrites to '@emote' + rest. DoCommand (423537) trims a trailing ',', looks the verb up in the case-insensitive hash, falls back to DoChannelCommand, then Event_Talk(line). InitializeCommands maps e/em/emote/me -> DoEmote. c/covassal/covassals/co-vassals, f/fellow/fellows/fellowship/g/group/party, m/monarch, p/patron and v/vassal/vassals map to DoStupidChannelHack. GetChannelID maps c* -> 0x1000000, m -> 0x4000, p -> 0x2000, v -> 0x1000 and f/g/party -> 0x800. In the OnChatCommand default (Say focus), PublicChat (426025) loops RemoveTextBetween('*','*') and ('<','>') and sends Event_Talk only if the remainder is non-empty. Pose (425512) replaces %p with 'his' when PropertyInt 0x71==1 (default 1), otherwise 'her', in otherEmote only. OpenAC citations verified: ChatInputParser.cs:100-115 reparses only known @ verbs; ChatCommandRouter.cs:90-93; RetailClientCommandCatalog.cs:474-477; ChatPoseCatalog.cs:106-117; RetailPublicChatParserTests.cs:23/32.
verify.corrections: (1) '@' must NOT simply become '/'. Only verbs in retail's client command table get rerouted, as OpenAC does. Any other '@line' must go to sendChat verbatim. In particular '@<soul-emote token>' must not hit holtburger's soul-emote catch-all, which is a non-retail convenience: retail DoEmote is plain Event_Emote, and retail '/wave' becomes Talk '@wave'. Unknown '@x' must not be rewritten. (2) Pose semantics: when ChatPoseTable resolves a token, retail ALWAYS sends Event_SoulEmote and the 'You ...' echo. RemoveTextBetween strips the token from the spoken text only when Pose returns 1, i.e. a motion command resolved. So run the soul-emote send for any non-null resolveSoulEmote, but strip only when motionFull !== 0. (3) A bare ':' or ';' (empty) sends nothing; DoEmote with no args returns without sending. (4) Retail replaces %p only in otherEmote, and defaults to 'his' when Gender is absent.
verify.implementation_notes: JS (no wasm): in routeSlashCommand, normalise first. If the message starts with ':' or ';', set message = '/emote ' + message.slice(1), and when the rest is empty return {dispatched:true, echo:null} without sending. If it starts with '@', compute the verb (lowercased, trailing ',' trimmed). Only when the verb is in RETAIL_CLIENT_VERBS (TELL/REPLY/RETELL/SAY aliases, EMOTE_ALIASES {e,em,emote,me}, CHANNEL_MAP keys, TURBINE_CMDS keys, ab) rewrite it to '/' + rest. Otherwise return {dispatched:false} so the index.html fall-through sends it verbatim. Match verbs case-insensitively with a trailing ',' trimmed. Route EMOTE_ALIASES through the existing /me branch. Add CHANNEL_MAP aliases: c/covassal/covassals/co-vassals -> 0x01000000; fellow/fellows/fellowship/g/group/party -> 0x800; monarch -> 0x4000; patron -> 0x2000; vassal/vassals -> 0x1000. Export a pure extractPoses(text, resolve) -> {spoken, poses:[resolved...]}. It scans each position for '*...*' then '<...>'. For each closed token where resolve(token) is non-null it records the pose. It strips the token (markers included) only when motionFull !== 0. Unclosed or unknown tokens stay literal. Refactor the soul-emote branch body into a reusable runSoulEmote(handle, resolved, token) that returns the echo, and call it for each pose. In index.html's plain-speech fall-through (Say focus only, i.e. no prefix), call extractPoses. If any poses are found, run them and append their 'You ...' echoes. Call sendChat(spoken) only if spoken.trim() is non-empty. In chat_log.js buildOutgoingLine, also pass ':'/';'-prefixed lines through verbatim. Wasm, %p only: in resolve_soul_emote, read `self.world.try_borrow().ok().and_then(|w| w.player_int_property(PropertyInt::Gender))` (holtburger_common PropertyInt::Gender = 113). Use 'his' if it is Some(1) or None, otherwise 'her'. Apply it to other_emote only, and leave my_emote untouched or with 'your'. Add a pure possessive_for_gender(Option<i32>) in chat_format.rs. No URL flag (HUD/input). Tests: test_slash_commands.mjs with a fake handle. '@tell Bob, hi' and '@T Bob, hi' call sendTell('Bob','hi'). '/e waves', ':waves' and ';waves' call sendEmote('waves'). '/c hi' calls sendChannel(0x01000000); '/party hi' calls sendChannel(0x800). '@loc' returns dispatched:false. '@wave' returns dispatched:false even when resolveSoulEmote('wave') is non-null. Using a stub resolver with motionFull 1/2 for one/two: extractPoses('a *one* b <two> c') gives spoken 'a  b  c' and poses [1,2]. 'x *nomotion* y', where the stub returns motionFull 0, keeps the text but records the pose. '*unknown* and *unfinished' stays literal. '*one*' alone gives spoken ''. Rust #[test]: possessive_for_gender(Some(1))=='his', (Some(2))=='her', (None)=='his'.

decomp_evidence: Handle_Communication__HearDirectSpeech (acclient.c:413504): when sender_id==target_id it prints "You think, \"%s\"" and sets no reply target.
