title: No client-side squelch filter (retail CanHear/IsSquelched), so squelched players' emotes and globally squelched message types still show
decomp_evidence: gmCCommunicationSystem::CanHear (acclient.c:434317): iid 0 always passes. Otherwise `if (msg_type == 1 || LogTextTypeEnumMapper::IsLegalChannel(msg_type)) v4 = SquelchDB::IsSquelched(db, iid, name, msg_type)`; a squelched sender returns 0, and senders beyond CPlayerSystem::GetRadarRadius() are also dropped. It is called from HearSpeech (acclient.c:413399, `CanHear(v8, ltt)`) and HearEmote (acclient.c:422504, `CanHear(sender, 0xCu)`), which also covers SoulEmote. Handle_Communication__TextboxString (422872) checks `gmCCommunicationSystem::IsSquelched(0, &account_name, ltt)` (global per-type squelch) before showing server text.
openac_evidence: OpenAC keeps the DB (src/AcDream.Core/Social/SquelchState.cs, replaced on SetSquelchDB in GameEventWiring.cs:393-399) and has the suppression hook (src/AcDream.Core/Chat/ChatSuppressionFilters.cs ShouldSuppress), but no CanHear predicate is wired (no IsSquelched/CanHear anywhere in src/). Retail is the only authority here.
holt_evidence: game_event.rs:1189-1203 SetSquelchDb calls publish_player_squelch_snapshot (lib.rs), which stores characters {target_guid, mask, is_account} plus globals_mask in latest_squelch (session/mod.rs:84, a LoopCtx field). The chat.rs EmoteText, SoulEmote, HearSpeech and ServerMessage arms never consult it. ACE Player.HandleActionEmote and HandleActionSoulEmote call `EnqueueBroadcast(msg, LocalBroadcastRange)` without a squelchType (only Talk passes ChatMessageType.Speech), so ACE does not filter emotes on the server. ACE SquelchManager.IsLegalChannel includes Emote, and SquelchDB.Contains uses bit `1 << (int)type` per character plus Globals. SquelchManager calls SendSquelchDB after each modify, so a client mirror stays current.
discrepancy: Squelching a harasser in holtburger still shows their /me and soul emotes, which retail hides. A global squelch by message type (e.g. squelching all Emote, or Combat server text) has no effect on lines the server doesn't filter.
proposed_change: Add a pure `can_hear(snapshot: Option<&SquelchSnapshot>, sender: u32, chat_type: u32) -> bool` in src/chat_format.rs. Sender 0 checks globals only. Use the legal-channel set from ACE/retail. An is_account entry for the sender blocks everything; otherwise block when the character mask or globals_mask has `1 << chat_type` set. Destructure latest_squelch in chat.rs and gate the EmoteText and SoulEmote arms (chat_type 12), HearSpeech/HearRangedSpeech (data.chat_type) and ServerMessage (sender 0) before pushing CHAT_RECEIVED and the matching OVERHEAD_SPEECH bubble. The radar-radius gate is optional and can come later.
files_to_change: apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs (make SquelchSnapshot fields reachable from chat_format, or pass masks in)
test_plan: Rust #[test]s in src/chat_format.rs: can_hear(None, x, 12) is true; a character entry with mask 1<<12 blocks Emote from that guid but not Speech(2); an is_account entry blocks every legal type; globals_mask 1<<6 (Combat) blocks sender 0 Combat text; a non-legal type (e.g. 0) always passes. The orchestrator runs `cargo test -p holtburger-web --lib chat_format`.

verify.reasons: In the decomp, gmCCommunicationSystem::CanHear (acclient.c:434317) returns 1 for iid 0. Otherwise it calls SquelchDB::IsSquelched when msg_type==1 or LogTextTypeEnumMapper::IsLegalChannel(msg_type), then drops senders whose physics object lies beyond GetRadarRadius. Call sites: HearSpeech (CanHear(v8, ltt)) and HearEmote (CanHear(sender, 0xC)), so SoulEmote is covered via HearEmote. HandleRangedTalkEvent (434662) uses IsSquelched(sender_id, name, ltt) plus ObjectsInRange. TextboxString (422872) shows a line only when IsSquelched(0, account_name, ltt)==0. SquelchDB::IsSquelched (714573) checks global squelch first, skips account/character checks for msg_type 17 (Spellcasting), then checks the account hash, then IsPlayerSquelched. IsLegalChannel (713311) = {2,3,6,7,0xC,0x10,0x11,0x12,0x13,0x15,0x16,0x17,0x18,0x19}, identical to ACE SquelchManager.IsLegalChannel. In holtburger, the chat.rs arms never read latest_squelch (only game_event.rs:1200 writes it, via publish_player_squelch_snapshot, which keeps filters[0] as mask plus is_account plus globals_mask). JS has no squelch filtering (rg over app/plugins/index.html/scene3d). On ACE: Player.cs:826/839 emote broadcasts pass no squelchType, so emotes are not filtered server-side; Talk passes ChatMessageType.Speech. SquelchDB.Contains / ToMask use 1<<type, with AllChannels = 0xFFFFFFFF. CharactersPlus sends account squelches as character entries with Account=true and an AllChannels mask. SquelchManager calls SendSquelchDB after each modify (lines 123/249/278). OpenAC has no CanHear/IsSquelched in src (rg), as stated.
verify.corrections: Refinements to the proposed can_hear: (1) sender 0 always passes CanHear. Global per-type squelch of server text is the separate TextboxString path, i.e. IsSquelched(0, ...). For ServerMessage, check globals_mask only, and only for legal types. (2) chat_type 17 (Spellcasting) checks globals only, never the character or account entries. (3) The order is globals, then is_account, then the character mask. (4) HearRangedSpeech is gated too, with IsSquelched plus a range check rather than radar radius. The radar and range gates can wait. SquelchSnapshot and SquelchEntry are #[cfg(target_arch=wasm32)] private structs in lib.rs (~30399), so chat_format must take primitive inputs. ACE already filters Speech and Tell server-side, so the client gate mainly adds Emote/SoulEmote and global-type filtering; double-filtering is harmless.
verify.implementation_notes: chat_format.rs: pub fn is_legal_squelch_channel(t:u32)->bool, matching {2,3,6,7,12,16,17,18,19,21,22,23,24,25}. Add pub fn can_hear(sender:u32, chat_type:u32, entry: Option<(u32 /*mask*/, bool /*is_account*/)>, globals_mask:u32)->bool. If sender==0, return true; ServerMessage uses a separate textbox_visible(chat_type, globals_mask) = !(legal(chat_type) && globals_mask & (1<<chat_type) != 0). If !(chat_type==1 || legal), return true. If globals_mask has the bit, return false. If chat_type==17, return true. If entry.is_account, return false. If entry.mask has the bit, return false. Otherwise true. In chat.rs, destructure latest_squelch from LoopCtx, and look up the entry by target_guid == sender in snapshot.characters (borrow, then drop before the pushes). Gate: EmoteText and SoulEmote with chat_type 12; HearSpeech and HearRangedSpeech with data.chat_type; ServerMessage with textbox_visible(data.chat_type). Suppress both the CHAT_RECEIVED push and its OVERHEAD_SPEECH companion. No URL flag (HUD; retail behaviour). Optionally add a `?clientSquelch=off` escape if the orchestrator wants one. Tests in chat_format.rs: can_hear(5, 12, None, 0) is true. With entry (1<<12, false), sender 5 is blocked for 12 but not for 2. An is_account entry blocks 2, 3 and 12. globals 1<<6 makes textbox_visible(6, 1<<6) false and textbox_visible(5, 1<<6) true. A non-legal type 0 always passes. chat_type 17 with entry mask 0xFFFFFFFF and globals 0 passes, while globals 1<<17 blocks it. The orchestrator runs `cargo test -p holtburger-web --lib chat_format`. Needs a wasm rebuild.

title: Held child inherits the wielder's obj_scale / ScaleHook / jump-squash scale through the three.js part node; retail draws the child at its own scale with an unscaled holding offset
decomp_evidence: CPhysicsObj::UpdateChild acclient.c:320039-320057: `Frame::combine(&new_frame, &v4->parts[part_index]->pos.frame, child_frame); CPhysicsObj::set_frame(child_obj, &new_frame);`. Frame is origin+quat only, so no scale reaches the child. CPhysicsObj::add_child :316729-316760 stores the raw holding Frame (`CHILDLIST::add_child(v3->children, obj, (Frame *)&v6[1].hash_next, part, where)`). The parent's scale only multiplies the anim-frame origin of its own parts: CPartArray::UpdateParts :326601 `Frame::combine(&parts[i]->pos.frame, frame, &v3->frame[v6], &v2->scale)` → Frame::combine(scale) :326563 `v5 = _f2->m_fOrigin.x * scale->x`. The child's mesh size comes only from its own part_array scale (CPartArray::SetScaleInternal :326182: gfxobj_scale = default_scale * this->scale). CPhysicsObj::SetScale :320622 and SetScaleStatic :319008 never touch children.
openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Core/Meshing/EquippedChildAttachment.cs:132 `Matrix4x4 childRoot = holdingFrame * parentPart;` (unscaled holding frame). :152-160: child visual = DefaultScale * partFrame, then `if (childScale != 1.0f) visualChildPart *= CreateScale(childScale)`, i.e. the child's own scale only. EquippedChildRenderController.cs:441 takes the scale from childSpawn.ObjScale. :638 rejects a parent world pose that carries scale (`Vector3.DistanceSquared(scale, Vector3.One) > 1e-6f`). Test tests/AcDream.Core.Tests/Meshing/EquippedChildAttachmentTests.cs:156 ChildRigidPoseExcludesDefaultScaleAndScalesOnlyOrigin.
holt_evidence: scene3d/entities.js:5003-5006 `inst._baseScale = ...objScale...; root.scale.setScalar(inst._baseScale)` puts the scale on the wielder ROOT. attachChildToParent :6716-6717 `mount.add(c.root)` under `p.parts[loc.partId]`, and :6736 `c.root.position.set(loc.ox, loc.oy, loc.oz)`. The comment at :6744 claims 'The wielder root may carry obj_scale; the child inherits it through the part node ... matches retail'. The decomp contradicts this. Other root-scale writers also reach the child: the jump squash `inst.root.scale.set(base, base, base * scaleZ)` :10290 and the _tickScaleHookTween root.scale writes. LSD sample: 467 creature weenies with DefaultScale≠1 and a wield createList, e.g. Guardian Golem 1.3, Gurog Soldier 1.3, Platinum Legion Castle Guard 1.2.
discrepancy: For a wielder with scale s, holtburger draws the weapon at s·s_child and places it s× farther from the hand bone. Retail draws it at s_child, offset by the raw holding frame from the (scaled) hand position. A 1.3× golem's sword is 30% too big and floats off the grip.
proposed_change: In attachChildToParent, after the mount, cancel the parent's uniform scale: `const ps = p._scaleNow || p.root.scale.x || 1; c.root.position.set(loc.ox/ps, loc.oy/ps, loc.oz/ps); c.root.scale.setScalar((c._baseScale || 1)/ps); c._attachLoc = loc;`. Add `_syncAttachedChildScale(parentInst)` to recompute this for every guid in parentInst._attachedChildren. Call it at the end of _tickScaleHookTween and after each runtime objScale change. For the jump squash, compensate only the uniform `base` term; the squash itself is cosmetic. In _detachChild, restore `c.root.scale.setScalar(c._baseScale || 1)`. Fix the misleading comment at :6744.
test_plan: New tests/held_child_scale.test.mjs. Load EntityManager the way test_a5_p3_root_motion.mjs does (harness/lib/scene3d_stubs.mjs entitiesToplevelPrelude + node_modules three). Build a parent with root.scale 1.3 and a part Group at (0,0,1), and a child with _baseScale 1. Stub _resolveHoldingLocation → {partId:0, ox:0.1, oy:0, oz:0, qw:1}, and stub _applyChildPlacementFrames/_preCreate. Call attachChildToParent.call(fake, …), then updateMatrixWorld. Assert c.root.getWorldScale ≈ (1,1,1). Assert the child's world offset from the part's world origin ≈ 0.1, not 0.13. Assert that after _detachChild the child's scale returns to _baseScale. Run: node tests/held_child_scale.test.mjs

verify.reasons: Re-read the decomp. CPhysicsObj::UpdateChild (acclient.c:320039-320057) does `Frame::combine(&new_frame, &v4->parts[part_index]->pos.frame, child_frame); CPhysicsObj::set_frame(child_obj, &new_frame)`. That is the 3-arg combine (origin+quat), so no scale reaches the child. add_child (:316729-316760) stores the raw holding Frame. CPartArray::UpdateParts (:326624) uses the scaled overload `Frame::combine(&parts[i]->pos.frame, frame, &v3->frame[v6], &v2->scale)`, and that overload (:326563) scales only the anim-frame origin (`_f2->m_fOrigin.x * scale->x`). So the hand position is scaled, but the child offset and the child mesh are not. CPhysicsObj::SetScale (:320622) only queues an FPHook or calls SetScaleInternal on the object's own part_array. In holtburger, entities.js:5003-5006 puts objScale on the wielder ROOT (`root.scale.setScalar(inst._baseScale)`). Part groups are direct children of root (`root.add(partGroup)` :4889). attachChildToParent mounts `mount.add(c.root)` under `p.parts[loc.partId]` (:6716-6717) and sets `c.root.position.set(loc.ox, loc.oy, loc.oz)` (:6736). Nothing compensates: an rg for scale near attach/child/held finds only the :6744 comment, which wrongly says 'matches retail'. The other root.scale writers are the jump squash `inst.root.scale.set(base, base, base*scaleZ)` (:10290) and the _tickScaleHookTween writes (:17083, :17089). OpenAC agrees with the decomp: EquippedChildAttachment.cs:132 `childRoot = holdingFrame * parentPart`, :152-160 child DefaultScale × own childScale only, and EquippedChildRenderController.cs:638 rejects a parent world pose that carries scale. Not tracked in PARITY-STATUS.json or the git log.
verify.corrections: `p._scaleNow` does not exist (no hits in entities.js). Use `p.root.scale.x`, or better the uniform base the writers use (`p._baseScale`, or the ScaleHook tween's current s). The '467 scaled armed creatures' LSD count was not re-verified; it does not change the conclusion. The jump squash is non-uniform `(base, base, base*scaleZ)` under a rotated part node, so only the uniform term can be cancelled with a child scale; the remainder shears the child. That is acceptable but should be stated. This is a change to the drawn size and offset of every held item on a scaled wielder, so it is a render change: it needs an eye test, and the owner may prefer proportional weapons.
verify.implementation_notes: Deferred until eye-test. When implemented, put it behind a flag such as `?heldChildScale=off`: module-level reader `!== "off"`, default ON, a row in url-flags.md, and `node scripts/lint-url-flags.mjs --strict` clean. (1) In attachChildToParent, after `mount.add(c.root)`, take `ps = p.root.scale.x || 1` (uniform term), set `c.root.position.set(loc.ox/ps, loc.oy/ps, loc.oz/ps)` and `c.root.scale.setScalar((c._baseScale||1)/ps)`, and keep `c._attachLoc = loc` for resync. In the loc===null branch, origin/ps is still 0. (2) Add `_syncAttachedChildScale(parentInst)` to iterate `parentInst._attachedChildren` and recompute from `_attachLoc`. Call it at the end of _tickScaleHookTween (both write sites :17083/:17089), after the jump-pose write (:10290, compensating `base` only), and after the R7 runtime objScale path in applyAppearance. (3) In _detachChild, restore `c.root.scale.setScalar(c._baseScale||1)`. (4) Rewrite the :6744 comment to cite UpdateChild :320039 / UpdateParts :326624. Test: tests/held_child_scale.test.mjs, loading EntityManager via harness/lib/scene3d_stubs.mjs entitiesToplevelPrelude as test_a5_p3_root_motion.mjs (app root) does. Parent root scale 1.3, part Group at (0,0,1), child `_baseScale` 1, stub `_resolveHoldingLocation` → {partId:0, ox:0.1,…, qw:1}, stub `_applyChildPlacementFrames`. Assert child world scale ≈ 1, offset from the part world origin ≈ 0.1, and _baseScale restored after _detachChild.

title: _lastAttach ledger re-mounts an item into its old wielder's hand even when the server re-creates it on the ground; retail takes a parent only from the PhysicsDesc
decomp_evidence: ACCObjectMaint CreateObject path acclient.c:391950-391961: `CObjectMaint::SetChildren(obj, physicsdesc); v16 = PhysicsDesc::get_parent_id(physicsdesc); if (v16) { ... CPhysicsObj::set_parent(obj, parent, PhysicsDesc::get_parent_location_id(..)); }`. The link is rebuilt only from the wire PhysicsDesc. CObjectMaint::SetChildren :310888-310930 begins with `CPhysicsObj::unparent_children(obj)` and then re-parents exactly the listed (child_id, location_id) pairs. No client-side memory re-parents an object.
openac_evidence: EquippedChildRenderController.OnSpawn (EquippedChildRenderController.cs:116-131) accepts a relation only from `spawn.ParentGuid`/`spawn.ParentLocation` (the CreateObject PhysicsDesc) or from queued ParentEvents (ParentAttachmentState.Enqueue :374-389). There is no remembered-parent replay.
holt_evidence: remove() entities.js:12408-12417 unlinks a removed child from its wielder but deliberately keeps `_lastAttach`. _replayLastAttach :7026-7036 runs on every spawn commit (:5344): `const last = this._lastAttach.get(g); ... if (inst && inst._attachedParentGuid == null && wielder) this.attachChildToParent(g, last.parentGuid, ...)`. It does this without checking whether the new CreateObject carried a world Position and no Parent. ACE sends observers a DeleteObject (not a ParentEvent/PickupEvent) when someone unequips: ACE Player_Tracking.cs:131-152 RemoveTrackedEquippedObject → `new GameMessageDeleteObject(worldObject)`. _tickDynamicLod (:14902+) does not skip attached children. It measures distance from the HAND-LOCAL `inst.root?.position` (:14942), and _respawnForLod (:14978) rebuilds such a child with a pose derived from those hand-local coordinates, relying on the same ledger to re-mount it.
discrepancy: Scenario: observer sees B wield sword S (ledger S→B). B unequips S to his pack (observer gets DeleteObject → remove(S), ledger kept). B then drops S on the ground (observer gets a fresh CreateObject with a Position and no Parent). _replayLastAttach mounts S back into B's hand, and the setPose attached-child guard then ignores every later position for S. Retail and OpenAC show S on the ground.
proposed_change: (1) In _replayLastAttach, child branch: if the spawned inst carries a world pose (`(inst.meta?.landblockId>>>0) !== 0 && !inst.meta?.heldChild`), `this._lastAttach.delete(g)` and return without replaying. In the mirror branch, skip and delete entries whose child meta has a world pose. Poseless and held-child spawns (ACE's parented CreateObject, the Rust-synthesized wieldedSpawn, and _makeHeldChildMeta) keep replaying. (2) In _tickDynamicLod, add `if (inst._attachedParentGuid != null) continue;` (EQUIP-3 at :4080-4100 already says a parented object has no distance of its own). This removes the only internal respawn that builds a world-pose meta for an attached child. applyAppearance already re-mounts through selfAttach. (3) Optional, follow-up, needs wasm: consume the parsed-but-unused parent PhysicsDesc `children` list (crates/holtburger-protocol/src/messages/object/messages/description.rs:836) in the objects.rs ObjectCreate arm. Emit kind=7 attaches for the listed children plus a 'children reset' for the parent (retail SetChildren), then retire the ledger.
test_plan: New tests/held_ledger_world_spawn.test.mjs. Load EntityManager through harness/lib/scene3d_stubs.mjs as test_a5_p3_root_motion.mjs does. Build a fake with `_lastAttach = new Map([[CHILD,{parentGuid:W,location:1,placement:1}]])`, entityMap {CHILD:{meta:{landblockId:0xA9B40021}, _attachedParentGuid:null}, W:{root:{}}} and a spy attachChildToParent. Call EntityManager.prototype._replayLastAttach.call(fake, CHILD, false). Assert the spy was not called and the ledger entry was deleted. Repeat with meta.landblockId 0 and assert it is called. A second case drives the _tickDynamicLod guard with an attached inst and asserts that lodFetch and _respawnForLod are not invoked.

verify.reasons: Holtburger: remove() (entities.js:12415-12418) only unlinks a removed child from `p._attachedChildren` and never touches `_lastAttach`. Only `_detachChild` deletes it (:6835). `_replayLastAttach` (:7026-7048) runs at every spawn commit (:5344) and, when `!hasParkedAttach`, re-mounts `last.parentGuid` whenever the wielder rig exists. It does not look at what the new CreateObject carried. objects.rs ObjectCreate (:545-580) emits a kind=7 only when `data.parent_id` is Some. A parentless world CreateObject emits no detach, so the ledger is the only authority applied. ACE flow for an observer: unequip-to-pack → Creature_Equipment.cs:456 `RemoveTrackedEquippedObject` → Player_Tracking.cs:151 `GameMessageDeleteObject` (PickupEvent commented out). A later drop from the pack sends a fresh world CreateObject, so the ledger re-mounts S in B's hand. After that, the setPose guard (:6301-6305) ignores every position for S. For the local player the kind:47 (Wielder→NULL) handler calls `attachChildToParent(child,0)` → _detachChild, which clears the ledger, so the defect is observer-side. The retail authority is stronger than cited: SmartBox::HandleCreateObject (acclient.c:145986-145994) skips enter_world only when the PhysicsDesc has a parent. For a same-instance re-create without a parent it goes to HandleReceivedPosition (which unset_parents, :145187) or DoPickupEvent (:146016-146044). CObjectMaint::DeleteObject (:309917) does unset_parent + destroy. The CreateObject tail (:391950-391961) only sets a parent from the PhysicsDesc. _tickDynamicLod (:14902-14965) has no attached-child skip and measures the hand-local `inst.root.position`. _respawnForLod (:14978-15009) does remove()+spawn() with a pose derived from it. Verified.
verify.corrections: The proposed '(landblockId>>>0) !== 0 && !heldChild' test is not a reliable 'on the ground' signal. ACE TrySetChild sets `item.Location = Location` (Creature_Equipment.cs:510), and the Position flag is written whenever Location != null (WorldObject_Networking.cs:470-471). That conflicts with the in-code EQUIP-3 claim (entities.js ~:4092) that parented CreateObjects arrive at landblock 0, so do not depend on either. Use spawn PROVENANCE instead. A wire KIND_SPAWN whose commit has no parked attach means the authoritative CreateObject had no Parent, because with wieldedSpawn ON every parented CreateObject emits kind=7 in the same batch and parks it. Retail then leaves the object unparented. Only the two internal respawn sites need ledger replay: applyAppearance :11797 (already backed by selfAttach) and _respawnForLod :15005. The '_tickDynamicLod' skip is a good companion. Measuring the child's world position (getWorldPosition) would be closer to retail than skipping, but skipping is the minimal safe change.
verify.implementation_notes: Flag `?wieldLedgerAuthority=off` (module-level reader next to readWieldPersistFlag, `!== "off"`, default ON, url-flags.md row). (1) Tag internal respawns: in applyAppearance before `await this.spawn(newMeta)` (:11797) and in _respawnForLod before :15005, set `newMeta._internalRespawn = true`. (2) In _replayLastAttach child branch (:7028-7037): if flag ON && `this._wieldedSpawn` && `!inst?.meta?._internalRespawn`, call `this._lastAttach.delete(g)` and skip the replay (hasParkedAttach=true keeps today's no-op). In the mirror loop (:7041-7047), skip and delete entries whose child inst was a wire spawn (`!c.meta?._internalRespawn`) and is currently unparented, since such a child was re-created by the server without a Parent. (3) In _tickDynamicLod add `if (inst._attachedParentGuid != null) continue;` next to the projectile skip (:14941). (4) Keep `?wieldedSpawn=off` behaviour unchanged, because there the ledger is the only re-mount. Test: new tests/held_ledger_wire_spawn.test.mjs (EntityManager via harness/lib/scene3d_stubs.mjs). Case A: fake with `_lastAttach=new Map([[C,{parentGuid:W,location:1,placement:1}]])`, `_wieldedSpawn=true`, entityMap {C:{meta:{}, _attachedParentGuid:null}, W:{root:{}}}, spy attachChildToParent. `_replayLastAttach.call(fake,C,false)` → spy not called and ledger entry deleted. Case B: same with meta._internalRespawn=true → spy called once. Case C: hasParkedAttach=true → no call and ledger kept. Case D: _tickDynamicLod with an attached inst and a stub lodFetch spy → spy not invoked. Run: node tests/held_ledger_wire_spawn.test.mjs.

title: ParentEvent/PickupEvent ignore instance + position stamps, and JS drops every position for a held item; retail gates on the stamps and lets a newer UpdatePosition un-parent the item
decomp_evidence: SmartBox::HandleParentEvent acclient.c:144512-144552: the parent's instance stamp must equal ts1 (newer → QueueBlobForObject, older → result 2/drop). The child must exist. SmartBox::DoParentEvent :143504-143528 applies only if the stamp is newer than `child->update_times[0]`, records it, then calls `set_parent(child, parent, child_location); SetPlacementFrame(child, placement_id, 1)`. HandlePickupEvent :144473-144508 and DoPickupEvent :143483-143500 use the same gate, then `unset_parent(object); leave_world(object)`. SmartBox::HandleReceivedPosition :145167-145196: after newer_event(POSITION) and the teleport check, `CPhysicsObj::unset_parent(object); if (!HasAnims(object)) SetPlacementFrame(object, placement_id, 1);` then MoveOrTeleport. title: Async attachChildToParent / _applyChildPlacementFrames have no per-child generation check, so a stale attach or placement can land after a newer detach, re-parent or remove

After it, the code only checks that both rigs still exist and re-parks the request if not; it never asks whether a newer request superseded this one. _detachChild (:6828) is synchronous. _applyChildPlacementFrames (:6913) awaits `fetchFn(sid, placement)` (:6927), then checks only `if (!c || !c.parts) return;` (:6950) before writing the frames for its own `placement`. Example 2: the child is removed meanwhile, and the resumed attach re-parks a stale request that can mount a later re-creation. Example 3: two attaches with different placements whose frame fetches resolve out of order leave the older grip pose on the parts, which is the B5 'vertical spear' symptom.

After every await, `if (this._attachGen.get(cGuid) !== gen) return;`, without re-parking. Pass gen into _applyChildPlacementFrames and re-check it after its await, together with `c._attachedParentGuid === pGuid && c._attachedPlacement === placement`. Delete the entry when the child is finally removed so the map does not grow.

After resuming it only checks that both rigs exist (:6702-6706) and re-parks if not. title: When the patron is the monarch, the snapshot has patron=None, so the panel shows 'Monarch', disables Break and enables Swear

title: Trade handler treats Decline, ClearTradeAcceptance and TradeFailure the same; retail clears only the decliner's flag and flushes both offers on ClearTradeAcceptance
decomp_evidence: ClientTradeSystem::Handle_Trade__Recv_DeclineTrade (acclient.c:410398): `if (source == player_id) _accepted = 0; else _p_accepted = 0;`. gmSecureTradeUI::RecvNotice_DeclineTrade (251359) resets only that side's button or indicator. gmSecureTradeUI::RecvNotice_ClearTradeAcceptance (251851) calls `gmSecureTradeUI::Reset(...)`. gmSecureTradeUI::Reset (251599) calls FlushTradeLists, which empties both item lists and queues the partner's non-owned items for destruction (251201), and sets the partner indicator to state 13. ApplyFailure (198-211) removes the item. Note that OpenAC ApplyClearAcceptance (213-223) also keeps the items; that is the same divergence, and the decomp wins.

In ACE (ace-server Player_Trade.cs:188-194), ClearTradeAcceptance() runs `ItemsInTradeWindow.Clear(); TradeAccepted=false;` and is called for both players when VerifyTrade_BusyState fails or a pack is full (356-357, 424-425). HandleActionDeclineTrade (307-323) clears only the decliner's TradeAccepted. VerifyTrade_Inventory (368-376) declines just the side whose offered item has gone, while both sides were accepted. The plugins/trade-panel.js:25-26 header already claims the 'ClearTradeAcceptance → Reset' semantics that the Rust code does not implement.

(b) When one side declines, holtburger also clears the other side's acceptance. ACE still has that side accepted, so the partner pressing Trade completes the exchange even though my window shows 'not accepted'. (c) TradeFailure should drop the rejected item from my list.

A plain 3D centre distance against 5.0+0.96 is a reasonable approximation. title: Retail's 0.2 s use throttle (ItemHolder::m_timeLastUsed) is inventory-only; world double-click, toolbar Use and radial Use can send several Use events within 200 ms

That single throttle is consumed by RuntimeItemInteraction.ActivateItem (RuntimeItemInteraction.cs:826) and by the world-use route (RuntimeWorldObjectUse.cs:157 TryConsumeUseThrottleForAutomation).
holt_evidence: apps/holtburger-web/plugins/inventory.js:590-601 `const ACTIVATE_THROTTLE_MS = 200; let lastActivateAt = -Infinity; ... if (now - lastActivateAt < ACTIVATE_THROTTLE_MS) return true;` is module-local and covers owned inventory rows only. scene3d/picking.js:1296-1302 (double-click → useObject), plugins/target-bar.js:538-551 (onUseClick → useObject) and plugins/radial-menu.js:536-543 (Use → useObject) are not throttled. Check trackedTargetYaw for a target due north, east and behind relative to the pivot (yaw matches the followYaw convention), and null for a coincident target. Add a static source assertion that camera.js calls _updateCombatTargetTracking and gates it on combatMode 2/4 and option 0x07.

verify.reasons:
Decomp:
- CPlayerModule::OnInitialize (~acclient.c:452803) and OnChanged case 7 call ClientCombatSystem::TrackTarget(ViewCombatTarget()).
- TrackTarget (:407978) sets m_bTrackingTarget and calls UpdateTargetTracking.
- UpdateTargetTracking (:407600): `if (m_bTrackingTarget && (combatMode==2||combatMode==4) && GetAttackTarget() && ObjectIsAttackable(t)) CameraSet::TrackTarget(cs,t) else CameraSet::TrackTarget(cs,0)`.
- It is re-run from RecvNotice_SelectionChanged (:408752) and from the combat-mode change (:408862).
- CameraSet::TrackTarget (:148758) calls SetTargetObject(gid) with target_offset (0,0,0.5), then SetTargetForOffset (:148214) sets LOOK_AT_PIVOT|LOOK_AT_OBJECT. That function does nothing when looking_down or in-head (offset 0,0.18,0).
- CameraManager::UpdateCamera (:147425) adds normalize(targetPos − pivot) to target_direction. Without LOOK_IN_DIRECTION the player direction is NOT added. It then calls `Frame::set_vector_heading(&pivot_frame, &pivot_direction); localtoglobal(&pivot_frame, viewer_offset)`. So the camera boom heading becomes the pivot→target direction, and the camera still looks at the pivot. This matches OpenAC RetailChaseCamera.ComputeTrackedHeading and CombatCameraTargetSource (verified).

Holtburger:
- rg over scene3d/ui/plugins finds option 0x07 only at options-panel.js:715.
- camera.js tick() calls _updateAutoFollow at :1058, which eases followYaw toward the player heading.
- computeMovementFromKeys confirms followYaw no longer steers WASD (player-local intent), so changing followYaw is camera-only.
- __sessionHandle.combatMode() exists (lib.rs:36536). entities.js _isAttackableTarget is at :8642.

Not in git log and not tracked.
verify.corrections:
- Retail REPLACES the player-heading term while it tracks (target_status has no LOOK_IN_DIRECTION bit), so _updateAutoFollow must be skipped while tracking is active. Otherwise the two eases fight.
- Retail does not track in first person or while looking down (SetTargetForOffset). Only melee (2) and missile (4) qualify, not magic (8).
- Retail's heading is the 3D pivot→target direction. A yaw-only approximation (atan2(dx,dy) in the camera's (sin,cos) forward convention) is acceptable but approximate.
- Retail keeps the user's viewer_offset rotation relative to the tracked heading. Holtburger's followYaw is absolute, so skipping the ease during right-drag plus the AUTOFOLLOW_GRACE_MS window is the practical equivalent.
- The option is default OFF in retail (0x80 is not in 0x50C4A54A), so bare-default behaviour does not change.
- File overlap: round-2 finding camera-5 also edits _updateAutoFollow in camera.js. Put both in the same lane.
verify.implementation_notes:
1. scene3d/camera_math.js: export pure `trackedTargetYaw(pivot, target)`.
   - dx = target.x − pivot.x, dy = target.y − pivot.y (AC coords).
   - Return null when Math.hypot(dx,dy) < 1e-4.
   - Otherwise return Math.atan2(dx, dy). camera.js forward is (sin yaw, cos yaw), so yaw = atan2(dx,dy) puts the camera behind the player looking at the target.
2. camera.js: add `_updateCombatTargetTracking(dt)` and call it before _updateAutoFollow in tick().
   - Return a boolean `tracking`. When true, skip _updateAutoFollow.
   - Gates:
     - COMBAT_TARGET_VIEW flag (`defaultOnUrlFlag`-style: `?combatTargetView=off` → reader `!== "off"`)
     - mode==='follow'
     - !(this._retailZoomOn && this._inHead)
     - option 0x07 via isCharacterOptionEnabled(0x07,false) from ui/ac_character_options.js. Cache it and refresh on pluginClient 'playerStatsUpdated', or read at most every ~250 ms.
     - handle.combatMode() is 2 or 4
     - sel = entityManager.getSelectedGuid/_selectedGuid is nonzero, and entityManager._isAttackableTarget(sel) is true
     - the target rig's world position is available (AC coords; add 0.5 m z for parity, which does not affect yaw)
   - Skip the ease, but still return tracking=true, while _followDragging or inside AUTOFOLLOW_GRACE_MS after a drag.
   - Ease: err wrapped to [-π,π]; followYaw += err * (1 − exp(−rate·dt)). Reuse _autoFollowRate or stiffnessFrac(this._camStiffness, dt).
3. Add a url-flags.md row for combatTargetView (default ON, `!== "off"`) and run `node scripts/lint-url-flags.mjs --strict` (cheap; not the gate).

Tests:
- Extend tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs (`node tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs`):
  - trackedTargetYaw for a target due north → 0, due east → π/2, due south → ±π, and coincident → null.
  - Static source assertions: camera.js contains `_updateCombatTargetTracking`, gates on combatMode 2/4 and option 0x07, reads `combatTargetView`, and skips _updateAutoFollow while tracking.

title: PlayerIsDead check always returns false in the CommandInterpreter port, so a dead local player can still walk, run and auto-run
decomp_evidence: CommandInterpreter::MovePlayer acclient.c:717800; first gate at :717828-717833: `if (vfptr[10]/*PlayerIsDead*/(v6)) { vfptr[9].OnAction/*LoseKeyboardFocus*/; vfptr[17]/*SetAutoRun*/(0,0); return; }` (vtable offsets from acclient.txt:292081-292133: 112=LoseKeyboardFocus, 120=PlayerIsDead, 204=SetAutoRun). TakeControlFromServer :716934-716940 also requires `!PlayerIsDead()`. PlayerIsDead :717695-717705 is `InqInterpretedMotionState(player)->forward_command == 0x40000011`. The interpreted state comes from the server's non-autonomous UpdateMotion: CPhysics::SetObjectMovement :311149-311193 unpacks it when `autonomous==0`. InterpretedMotionState::UnPack defaults forward_command to Ready (0x41000003) when the flag is absent (:333493). Net effect: from the server's Dead motion until its next Ready, every movement key is refused and auto-run is cleared.
openac_evidence: OpenAC is not a model for the gate itself: PlayerMovementController.TakeControlFromServer (src/AcDream.Runtime/Gameplay/PlayerMovementController.cs:919-925) has no PlayerIsDead check. It does feed every local UpdateMotion's autonomy into the controller: LiveEntityNetworkUpdateController.cs:389 calls `SetLastMoveWasAutonomous(update.IsAutonomous)`, which sets `_controlledByServer = !autonomous` (PlayerMovementController.cs:1190-1194), then applies the motion through the player's motion interpreter (:401-409).
holt_evidence: The gate is ported faithfully but cannot fire. command_interpreter.rs:1298-1302 is `if self.player_is_dead(seams) { self.lose_keyboard_focus(seams); self.set_auto_run(seams, 0, false); return; }`, and :832-834 `player_is_dead` reads `seams.player_forward_command() == Some(MOTION_COMMAND_DEAD)`. But the production seam at crates/holtburger-core/src/client/movement/system.rs:9931-9933 is `fn player_forward_command(&self) -> Option<u32> { None // local player death routes through the wire lane; never Dead here }`. No 'wire lane' gate exists either: player/mutations.rs:353-359 only does `if let Some(forward) = invalid.state.forward_command { self.update_current_substate_from_low16(..) }`, and expand_motion_command_low16 (player/types.rs:129-344) has no 0x0011 arm (`_ => None` at :344), so Dead is never recorded. I found no dead check in the JS input modules either. ACE does not gate movement while dead: GameActionMoveToState.Handle (~/ace-server .../GameActionMoveToState.cs:17-35) runs OnMoveToState, SetRequestedLocation and BroadcastMovement with no IsDead check.
discrepancy: Retail refuses all movement input (and clears auto-run) while the interpreted forward_command is Dead. holtburger lets W, Q/E and auto-run drive a dead player. During ACE's death window (deathAnim + 1 s; Player_Death.cs:226-233) the client moves and sends MoveToState. ACE re-broadcasts it, so observers see the corpse-posed player stand up and run. The local JS predictor's WalkForward/RunForward counts as a 'revival' in the death-hold guard (entities.js:10687-10697), so the local rig stands up too. And CreateCorpse uses the player's current PhysicsObj.Position (Creature_Death.cs:493), so a player can move where their corpse drops.
proposed_change: (a) Give the local player the retail interpreted forward command. Add `PlayerState::server_forward_command: u32` (default 0x4100_0003). In `apply_self_update_motion` (mutations.rs), for every accepted non-autonomous `MovementTypeData::Invalid` envelope, set it to `invalid.state.forward_command.map(|c| expand(c.raw()).unwrap_or(0x4000_0000 | c.raw() as u32)).unwrap_or(0x4100_0003)`. A missing forward command means Ready, as in retail UnPack. Add `0x0011 => Some(0x4000_0011)` (Dead) to expand_motion_command_low16. is_action_motion_command already excludes class-0x40 Dead, so the action overlay is unaffected. Do NOT reuse `current_substate`: land()/begin_fall() overwrite it locally (types.rs:2187, :2212), which would reopen the gate after a mid-air death. (b) In SystemInterpreterSeams (system.rs:9931), return `Some(self.world.player.server_forward_command)`. This brings MovePlayer's LoseKeyboardFocus + SetAutoRun(0) refusal and TakeControlFromServer's guard online. Reset the field on world/session reset. ACE's post-teleport SetCombatMode(NonCombat) sends NonCombat+Ready (Player_Death.cs:255, Creature_Combat.cs:113-114), which clears it.
test_plan: Rust #[test] `apply_self_update_motion_tracks_dead_then_ready` in crates/holtburger-world/src/player (tests module): a non-autonomous Invalid envelope with forward 0x0011 sets 0x40000011; a following envelope with forward None sets 0x41000003. Rust #[test] `cmd_interp_refuses_movement_while_local_player_dead` in crates/holtburger-core/src/client/movement/system/tests.rs, following the existing cmd-interp tests that call `world.scene.set_local_server_controlled(true)`: after the Dead envelope, a WalkForward press edge leaves the drive idle and auto_run false, with no MoveToState; after a Ready envelope the same press drives. The orchestrator runs it once: `capped-build cargo test -p holtburger-core cmd_interp_refuses_movement_while_local_player_dead` and `-p holtburger-world apply_self_update_motion_tracks_dead`.

title: Local rig stays in the Dead pose after resurrection: the server's NonCombat Ready that ends death is dropped by the local-locomotion skip
decomp_evidence: CPhysics::SetObjectMovement acclient.c:311149-311193: a non-autonomous movement for the local player is always unpacked (`if (autonomous==0 || !is_player) { last_move_was_autonomous = autonomous; unpack_movement(...) }`). The server's interpreted Ready therefore replaces Dead in the player's interpreted state and the player stands up. The client never ignores a server-forced Ready for itself; only autonomous echoes are bookkeeping-only (:311186-311190).
openac_evidence: LiveEntityNetworkUpdateController.cs:384-409 applies EVERY local-player UpdateMotion (autonomous or not) through `_remoteInboundMotion.Apply(update, _playerController.Movement, ...)` after `SetLastMoveWasAutonomous(update.IsAutonomous)`. A server Ready after Dead therefore reaches the local motion interpreter and sequencer.
holt_evidence: loop.js:254 `const FORCE_MOTION_LOCAL_ON = true;`. :270-273 the predictor-owned set includes 0x0003 (Ready). :3704-3708 `forceLocal = FORCE_MOTION_LOCAL_ON && !isAuto && !isLocalGaitLocomotionCmd(motionCmd)`. So the local Dead (0x11) is forced through to setMotion, but the later non-autonomous Ready is not. It falls to :3723-3729 `em.setLocalStance(motionGuid, st)`. setLocalStance (entities.js:11419-11471): Dead was sent in NonCombat (ACE Player_Death.cs:185-186) and the resurrect motion is also NonCombat, so `!changed` → stamp only (:11460-11465) and no Ready is issued. The rig stays in the death hold (entities.js:10687-10697 refuses all but Ready/Walk/Run). The player death-state clear (:10840-10847) only runs on a later non-Dead setMotion. cancelOneShotOverlaysForGuid on teleport is a no-op (entities.js:13358).
discrepancy: Retail: the server's post-teleport NonCombat/Ready (ACE ThreadSafeTeleportOnDeath → SetCombatMode(NonCombat) → HandleSwitchToPeaceMode → ExecuteMotionPersist(new Motion(NonCombat)); Player_Death.cs:255, Creature_Combat.cs:113-114) stands the player up at the lifestone. holtburger: the avatar lies in the death pose at the lifestone until the player gives input that produces Ready/Walk/Run. A pure turn or strafe is refused by the death-hold guard, so the corpse-posed body rotates or slides.
proposed_change: In loop.js `_armMotion`, also force a NON-autonomous locomotion-class command onto the local rig while that rig is death-held: `forceLocal = FORCE_MOTION_LOCAL_ON && !isAuto && (!isLocalGaitLocomotionCmd(motionCmd) || em.isDeathHeld?.(motionGuid))`. Add `EntityManager.isDeathHeld(guid)`, returning `inst._unifiedSeq?.deathHold === true || ((inst.lastMotionCommand ?? 0) & 0xffff) === CMD_LOW_DEAD`. The predictor's B9 protection is unchanged outside death because autonomous echoes and live-player locomotion still skip. Put the decision in a pure helper `shouldForceLocalMotion({isLocal, isAuto, motionCmd, deathHeld})` in scene3d/death_hold.js so it can be unit-tested. Pairs with death-1: once input is gated while dead, this server Ready is the ONLY thing that revives the local rig.
test_plan: Extend tests/death_hold.test.mjs (run: `node tests/death_hold.test.mjs` from apps/holtburger-web). Cases: shouldForceLocalMotion({isLocal:true,isAuto:false,motionCmd:0x0003,deathHeld:true}) === true; the same with deathHeld:false === false (B9 preserved); isAuto:true with deathHeld:true === false; motionCmd 0x0011 (Dead) non-auto === true (unchanged).

title: Selection on a dying creature outlives its server DeleteObject for seconds (death-hold/ragdoll), delaying auto-target and aiming attacks at a deleted guid
decomp_evidence: The server delete removes the weenie: ACCObjectMaint::DeleteObject acclient.c:390928-390937. ACCWeenieObject::Remove :438580-438606: `if (id == selectedID) { selectedID = 0; prevSelectedID = prevSelectedValidID = id; CM_UI::SendNotice_SelectionChanged(); ... }`. The notice reaches ClientCombatSystem::RecvNotice_SelectionChanged (:408741-408783), which calls ClientCombatSystem::AutoTarget (:408690-408735) when the selection is empty in melee/missile with the AutoTarget option on. I found no Dead-motion-triggered clear; retail keeps the dying creature selected until the delete, then lets go immediately.
openac_evidence: OpenAC clears even EARLIER, on the Dead motion itself: RuntimeActionState.cs:263-264 `OnCreatureDied → CombatTarget.OnMotionApplied(objectId, MotionCommand.Dead)`, and RuntimeCombatTargetState.cs:43-52 clears the selection with reason CombatTargetDied, after which OnSelectionChanged (:61-82) auto-targets. That is earlier than retail; use retail's delete timing, not OpenAC's.
holt_evidence: The selection is cleared only inside `EntityManager.remove()` (entities.js:12376-12400: `if ((this._selectedGuid >>> 0) === g && g !== 0) { this._selectedGuid = 0; ... this._selRemovedGuid = g; ...}`). For a dying creature, loop.js `_armRemove` does not call remove at the server delete. A handoff-claimed creature returns at :3512-3516 and is removed later by finishReveal (entities.js:12339, after the collapse plus up to 8×500 ms ragdoll settle). Otherwise it is deferred via `setTimeout(fire, ...)` (:3576), polling up to DEATH_CLAIM_WAIT_LIVE_MS = 9000 / SETTLED 4000 (death_hold.js:23-24). Ragdoll is on by default (ragdoll.js:57-60, `!== "off"`). `_tickSelectionRules` (entities.js:8752-8757) would also re-select a guid still in entityMap (`if (this.entityMap.has(gone)) this._commitSelection(gone)`).
discrepancy: After a kill, holtburger keeps the deleted creature selected for the length of the visual hold. Auto-target to the next attacker or closest monster is delayed. noteAttacked() skips auto-target because the selection is non-zero (entities.js:8709). A queued attack, cast or Use goes to a guid the server and wasm no longer know (the same failure the F16-4 comment at 12376-12381 describes for despawns). Retail drops the selection at the delete.
proposed_change: Split the selection-release block out of `remove()` into `EntityManager.releaseSelectionOnServerDelete(g)`: clear `_selectedGuid`, set `_prevSelectedGuid`/`_selRemovedGuid`, clear selectionBracketLayer and emit selectionChanged. Call it from loop.js `_armRemove` at the TOP, i.e. at the real server delete, before both the handoff early-return and the deferral. Keep remove() calling it (idempotent). In `_tickSelectionRules`, only re-select a still-mapped guid when `!inst._removePending && !inst._corpseHandoffGuid`, otherwise run `_autoTarget("notice")`. Put the predicate in death_hold.js as `shouldReselectAfterRemoval(inst)`. The visual death-hold, ragdoll and corpse reveal are untouched.
test_plan: Add to tests/death_hold.test.mjs: shouldReselectAfterRemoval({_removePending:true}) === false; ({_corpseHandoffGuid:0x123}) === false; ({}) === true (LOD re-create still re-selects). Run `node tests/death_hold.test.mjs`. Optionally add a targeted EntityManager-stub test, tests/death_selection_release.test.mjs: after releaseSelectionOnServerDelete(g) with entityMap still holding g, `_selectedGuid === 0` and `_selRemovedGuid === g`.

verify.reasons: Decomp: ACCObjectMaint::DeleteObject (:390924-390937) → CObjectMaint::DeleteObject, which calls the weenie's Remove virtual. ACCWeenieObject::Remove (:438580-438610) does `if (id == selectedID) { selectedID = 0; prevSelectedID = prevSelectedValidID = id; CM_UI::SendNotice_SelectionChanged(); ...}`. RecvNotice_SelectionChanged (:408741) → AutoTarget in combat modes 2/4 with the option on. Holtburger: the only selection release on despawn is inside EntityManager.remove() (entities.js:12376-12400). loop.js _armRemove (:3493-3590) returns early for a handoff-claimed rig (:3512-3516; removal happens later in finishReveal at entities.js:12339, after up to 8×500 ms ragdoll-settle retries) or defers through setTimeout/deathHoldVerdict polling (DEATH_CLAIM_WAIT_LIVE_MS 9000 / SETTLED 4000, death_hold.js:23-24). Ragdoll is default-on (ragdoll.js ragdollEnabled `!== "off"`). noteAttacked (entities.js:8707-8710) skips auto-target while the selection is non-zero. _tickSelectionRules (:8751-8758) re-selects a removed guid that is still in entityMap. Not tracked in PARITY-STATUS.
verify.corrections: (1) Release early only on the death-deferral paths (the `typeof inst._deathAt === "number"` block in _armRemove). Every other KIND_REMOVE already calls em.remove synchronously, and releasing at the top of _armRemove changes nothing for them. (2) The _tickSelectionRules guard is required, not optional. Without it the next tick re-commits the still-mapped dying guid. (3) Cycle/auto-target candidates exclude only `_deadFrozen` (entities.js:8421/8440). _deadFrozen is set only by _freezeDeadReckon, which runs when the unified death bake succeeds or on a corpse claim (:11026, :12281). If the death anim is off or the bake falls back, a delete-deferred rig could be re-picked by 'closest'. Also skip `_removePending` and `_corpseHandoffGuid` there. (4) 'Attacks go to a deleted guid' is the F16-4 failure mode described in the remove() comment. I did not trace the attack-send path, so treat it as the likely consequence, not a verified one.
verify.implementation_notes: entities.js: extract the block at :12376-12400 into `releaseSelectionOnServerDelete(g)`. If `(this._selectedGuid>>>0) === g && g !== 0`: set _selectedGuid=0, _prevSelectedGuid=g, _selRemovedGuid=g, call selectionBracketLayer.setTarget(0,null,null) and emit selectionChanged {guid:0, prevGuid:g}. It is idempotent: a second call is a no-op because _selectedGuid is already 0. remove() calls it in place of the inline block. loop.js _armRemove: inside `if (inst && typeof deadAt === "number")`, call `em.releaseSelectionOnServerDelete?.(g)` first, before both the handoff early-return and shouldDeferDeathRemove. The release must happen in the same synchronous call that sets `_removePending` (or after `_corpseHandoffGuid` exists), so the next-tick guard sees it. _tickSelectionRules (:8752-8758): replace `if (this.entityMap.has(gone)) this._commitSelection(gone)` with `const gi = this.entityMap.get(gone); if (gi && shouldReselectAfterRemoval(gi)) this._commitSelection(gone); else this._autoTarget("notice");`. In scene3d/death_hold.js add `export function shouldReselectAfterRemoval(inst) { return !!inst && !inst._removePending && !inst._corpseHandoffGuid; }`. In _gatherCycleCandidates (both loops) add `|| inst._removePending || inst._corpseHandoffGuid` to the `_deadFrozen` skip. Flag `?deathSelectRelease=off` (default ON) → legacy timing. Run `node tests/death_hold.test.mjs`. No wasm rebuild. The visual death hold, ragdoll and corpse reveal are untouched; only the HUD selection brackets drop earlier.

title: Corpse-handoff search has no local-player exclusion; a claim would remove the local rig, which wasm never re-spawns
decomp_evidence: Retail has no client-side link between corpse and creature. The corpse is its own CreateObject, and an object leaves the client only through the server delete (ACCObjectMaint::DeleteObject acclient.c:390928-390937 → ACCWeenieObject::Remove :438580). The local player object is never deleted on death; it stays and is teleported.
openac_evidence: OpenAC records deaths per guid and incarnation and never tears down an entity because of a death fact. RuntimeCreatureDeathState.cs:18-19 (incarnation-keyed `_dead`) and :59-63 (`ObserveSpawn` clears any stale fact for a re-used guid). Removal follows only server Delete/Withdraw (RuntimeCreatureDeathEntityFollower.cs:22-34).
holt_evidence: _tryCorpseDeathHandoff (entities.js:12215-12235) accepts any entity with a numeric `_deathAt` within 4 m (8 m when the ragdoll is live) and the time window; nothing checks `_isLocalPlayerGuid`. The local Dead does stamp `_deathAt`: loop.js:3704-3708 forces the local non-autonomous Dead through to setMotion, and entities.js:10849-10851 stamps `inst._deathAt` with no local guard (only carnage/ragdoll are local-excluded at :10856, :10864). On a claim: :12279-12282 snaps and freezes the rig and sets `_corpseHandoffGuid`, then finishReveal calls `this.remove(creatureGuid)` (:12339). The local KIND_SPAWN is emitted once per session (src/session/messages/objects.rs:294-302, `skip_local_player_spawn = is_local_player && *local_player_spawn_emitted`), so a JS-removed local rig is never recreated.
discrepancy: ACE creates the player's corpse at the player's own physics position (Creature_Death.cs:493), deathAnim+1 s after Dead, and starts the teleport in the same action (Player_Death.cs:231-233). If the corpse spawn commits before the destination UpdatePosition moves the local rig, d≈0 and the window is open, so the corpse claims the LOCAL player and the reveal deletes the avatar. The outcome depends on a race (corpse spawn latency vs teleport position), so it may be intermittent. Remote players are safe because they are deleted and recreated by the server on teleport.
proposed_change: In the candidate loop of `_tryCorpseDeathHandoff`, add `if (this._isLocalPlayerGuid(inst.guid >>> 0)) continue;`. The local player is not ragdolled and its corpse should just show with its authored pose. Optionally also skip ODF-player rigs whose server delete has not arrived (`(inst.meta?.objDescFlags & 0x8) && !inst._removePending`), since a living player object persists across death. As belt-and-braces, make `remove()` refuse the local guid unless it is called from the server-delete/session-teardown path.
test_plan: Extract the per-candidate test into a pure `isCorpseHandoffCandidate({hasDeathAt, claimed, isLocal, isPlayerRig, removePending, inWindow, d2, maxD2})` in scene3d/death_hold.js and add cases to tests/death_hold.test.mjs (`node tests/death_hold.test.mjs`): a local rig at d2=0 inside the window → false; a dying creature at d2=0 → true; a player rig without removePending → false.

verify.reasons: _tryCorpseDeathHandoff (entities.js:12215-12245) accepts any entity with a numeric _deathAt inside the window and radius. It has no _isLocalPlayerGuid or ODF_PLAYER check. The local Dead stamps _deathAt (entities.js:10849-10851); only carnage and ragdoll are local-excluded (:10856, :10864). The window is endAt + DEATH_CORRELATE_GRACE_MS = 4000 (:2259). ACE creates the player corpse at deathAnim+1 s (Player_Death.cs:226-233), so the corpse arrives inside the window. The call site (entities.js ~:5150-5166) runs the handoff for every ODF_CORPSE spawn. On a claim, the code snaps and freezes the rig, sets _corpseHandoffGuid, and finishReveal calls `this.remove(creatureGuid)` (:12339). remove() has no local guard. The local KIND_SPAWN is emitted once (objects.rs:294-302 skip_local_player_spawn), and loop.js has no re-create path. Whether the local claim actually wins depends on a race I could not test. ACE Teleport (Player_Location.cs:686-694) sends PlayerTeleport plus an immediate 'fake' UpdatePosition at the destination right after CreateCorpse, so the local rig usually moves before the async corpse bake commits. The code defect is confirmed; how often it triggers is not.
verify.corrections: The finding's claim that 'remote players are safe because they are deleted and recreated by the server on teleport' is not supported. ACE's DO/CO refresh in HandlePreTeleportVisibility is disabled by default (`teleport_visibility_fix` < 1 → return). A remote player who resurrects within an observer's view keeps the same object with only UpdatePositions, and holtburger never re-creates a JS-removed rig. Remote player rigs ARE ragdolled (RAGDOLL_ON && !local) and claimable, so finishReveal can delete a living remote player's rig for the rest of their visibility. Fixing that (do not remove an ODF_PLAYER rig in finishReveal unless `_removePending`, or exclude it from candidates) changes how gore/ragdoll player corpses are presented. Treat it as a separate flagged follow-up that needs an eye-test, not part of this safe change.
verify.implementation_notes: Safe part (local only): in scene3d/death_hold.js add the pure `isCorpseHandoffCandidate({hasDeathAt, claimed, isLocal, inWindow, d2, maxD2})`. It returns false if !hasDeathAt, claimed or isLocal; otherwise `inWindow && d2 < maxD2`. In entities.js _tryCorpseDeathHandoff's candidate loop add `if (this._isLocalPlayerGuid(inst.guid >>> 0)) continue;` (or route through the helper). Apply the same skip in the diagnostic 'nearest' loop so the log does not name the local player. Belt-and-braces (optional): in finishReveal, `if (this._isLocalPlayerGuid(creatureGuid)) { /* unhide corpse, clear claim */ } else this.remove(creatureGuid);`. Tests: tests/death_hold.test.mjs: isLocal:true at d2=0 inside the window → false; a dying creature at d2=0 inside the window → true; claimed → false; d2 ≥ maxD2 → false. Run `node tests/death_hold.test.mjs`. No wasm rebuild, no flag needed (pure robustness guard). Follow-up, NOT safe now: the remote ODF_PLAYER handling described in corrections, behind `?playerCorpseHandoff=off`.

title: Missing retail 'unopened corpse' selection and use actions and the opened-corpse list
decomp_evidence: UI_SELECTION_TYPE has SELECTION_TYPE_UNOPENED_CORPSE = 5 (acclient.h:3041-3050). title: Absent RadarBehavior falls back to an ODF/itemType heuristic, so creature-typed props retail hides show on the radar

LSD has 357 creature-typed weenies with no PropertyInt 133, for example Exploration Marker, Arena Bell, Northern Pedestal, Yellow Lever, Shrine of the Eye of T'thuun and Strange Crystal. A handle with no objectIntProperty and itemType 0x10 gives true (the stale-pkg fallback). `() => 4` with odf 0x80 gives false. Run: node test_radar_projection.mjs; node tests/target_cycle.test.cjs.

title: Radar reads spawn-time meta.objDescFlags / meta.radarBlipColor, so other players' PK colour+shape go stale after a PK status change
decomp_evidence: ACCWeenieObject::OnStatUpdated(int) (acclient.c:438720) handles `case 0x86u: PublicWeenieDesc::SetPlayerKillerStatus(&this->pwd, val);` (:438785), `case 0x5Fu: this->pwd._blipColor = val;` (:438779) and `case 0x85u: this->pwd._radar_enum = val;` (:438782). SetPlayerKillerStatus (acclient.c:470685) rewrites the 0x20/0x200000/0x2000000 bits. gmRadarUI::OnQualityChanged (acclient.c:263725) then calls UpdateRadarLook (GetBlipColor + GetBlipShape) for that object, or for every blip when the change is on the player.
openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Core/Items/ClientObjectTable.cs:725-728 applies PlayerKillerStatusBitfield.Apply to item.PublicWeenieBitfield on an int-134 update (the live model). OpenAC's own RadarSnapshotProvider.cs:122 (`uint pwd = spawn.ObjectDescriptionFlags`) still reads spawn flags, so it has the same bug and only shows how to keep the data current.
holt_evidence: plugins/radar.js:355 `const odf = (meta?.objDescFlags ?? callNum(sh, "objectDescFlags", guid) ?? 0) >>> 0;`, where meta is the scene's spawn-time meta; only a re-spawn sets meta.objDescFlags (entity_update_clone.js:114). radar.js:363-367 caches `meta.radarBlipColor` once and never refreshes it. The wasm side is already live: crates/holtburger-world/src/handlers/properties.rs:89-92 runs `refresh_pk_bits(...)` on PublicUpdatePropertyInt, which updates Entity.flags, and src/lib.rs:36728 `object_desc_flags` returns `e.flags.bits()`. ACE sends PK changes only as PublicUpdatePropertyInt(PlayerKillerStatus) (PKModifier.cs:173, Player_Death.cs:966/971/1018).
discrepancy: When another player changes PK status (PK altar, or the temporary NPK after a PK death), the radar keeps the colour and shape from spawn time: red X versus white +, pink versus white. The local player's own bits come fresh from wasm (`_slow.player`), so the mutual-PK X test mixes fresh and stale data. A live RadarBlipColor update (int 95) is likewise ignored for the life of the entity.
proposed_change: In radarInfoFor, use wasm first: `const wf = callNum(sh, 'objectDescFlags', guid); const odf = ((wf !== undefined && wf !== 0) ? wf : (meta?.objDescFlags ?? 0)) >>> 0;`. Read the blip colour live: `const bc = callNum(sh, 'objectIntProperty', guid, 95); blipColor = bc !== undefined ? (bc >>> 0) : (meta?.radarBlipColor ?? callNum(sh, 'entityRadarBlipColor', guid) ?? 0);`, and stop writing it permanently into meta. Optionally clear the `_info` entry for a guid when a PropertiesUpdated event for int 95/133/134 arrives, instead of waiting out the 2 s INFO_TTL. Put this in a small exported pure helper, e.g. `resolveRadarLook(sh, guid, meta)`, so it can be tested. The entities.js:8014-8024 bracket tint has the same stale meta and could use the same helper.
test_plan: Export the helper from radar.js and add cases to test_radar_projection.mjs. A fake handle returning objectDescFlags 0x28 (Player|PK) with meta {objDescFlags: 0x08} gives odf 0x28, and blipShapeFor against a PK player gives X. A handle returning 0 (unknown guid) falls back to meta. objectIntProperty(95) = 8 gives the yellow blip colour even when meta.radarBlipColor = 0. Run: node test_radar_projection.mjs. The Rust side is already pinned by properties.rs pk_status_tests.
already_tracked: no (Rust half fixed: properties.rs refresh_pk_bits; JS radar still reads spawn meta)

verify.reasons:
Decomp re-read. ACCWeenieObject::OnStatUpdated(int) (acclient.c:438720) handles `case 0x5Fu: this->pwd._blipColor = val;`, `case 0x85u: this->pwd._radar_enum = val;` and `case 0x86u: PublicWeenieDesc::SetPlayerKillerStatus(&this->pwd, val);`. SetPlayerKillerStatus (:470685) rewrites the 0x20, 0x2000000 and 0x200000 bits (4 is PK, 0x40 PK-lite, 0x20 free-PK, anything else clears them). gmRadarUI::OnQualityChanged (:263725) recomputes GetBlipColor and GetBlipShape for every blip when the change is on the player, and otherwise calls UpdateRadarLook for that object. Retail's SetSelected computes GetBlipColor from the live pwd at selection time, so a live read at selection matches retail. title: Debug snapshot object rebuilt every 25 ms radar tick (per-blip hex strings + token style reads) with no consumer
decomp_evidence: n/a (perf). Retail gmRadarUI::UseTime (acclient.c:264347) repaints every 0.025 s and keeps no extra per-tick state beyond m_aRadarInfos.
openac_evidence: src/AcDream.App/UI/Layout/RadarSnapshotProvider.cs reuses `_blipScratch` and `_candidateScratch` lists; its comment says a list per refresh 'was one of the last per-frame allocations left'.
holt_evidence: plugins/radar.js:884 `_lastSnapshot = { ... tokens: Object.fromEntries([...].map((d) => [d, { left: parseInt(tokens[d].style.left, 10), ... }])), blips: drawn.map((b) => ({ guid: `0x${b.guid.toString(16).padStart(8, "0")}`, ... })) }` runs on every update() (40 Hz). Its only reader is `window.__radar.snapshot()` (debug; no other references in the repo).
discrepancy: About 40 snapshot objects per second, plus one string and one object per blip, are allocated only for a debug hook nobody calls in normal play. That is avoidable GC churn on a HUD loop already tuned for perf (commit 7d99b68a).
proposed_change: Store the raw per-tick values (source, heading, range, cellId, coordsText, the `drawn` array reference, locked) in a small reused record and build the formatted JSON inside `snapshot()` on demand.
test_plan: node test_radar_projection.mjs (pure maths unchanged). The orchestrator's later live check: `window.__radar.snapshot()` returns the same shape as before.

verify.reasons: radar.js:884-897 rebuilds `_lastSnapshot` on every update(). That allocates the snapshot object, the 4-entry tokens map with parseInt of `tokens[d].style.left/top`, and, for each blip, an object plus a padded hex guid string. The only reader is `window.__radar.snapshot()` (radar.js:936-939), which already deep-copies with JSON.parse/stringify. An rg over external/holtburger (excluding pkg/node_modules) finds no other `__radar` consumer apart from the unverified round-2 JSON. update() runs from rAF gated by UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS = 25 (:102, :904). OpenAC RadarSnapshotProvider reuses scratch lists. This is a real but small amount of garbage-collector churn.
verify.corrections: The rate is not a fixed 40 Hz. A rAF gated at 25 ms runs about every second frame on a 60 Hz display (about 30 Hz), and approaches 40 Hz only on high-refresh displays. Reading `element.style.left` reads the inline style declaration and does not force a style recalc (unlike the computed-style read fixed in 7d99b68a), so the cost is allocation only, not layout. Severity LOW is right.
verify.implementation_notes:
1. In the mount closure, replace the per-tick object literal with in-place writes to a module-level reused record. Example: `_snapRaw.source = source; _snapRaw.heading = heading; _snapRaw.range = range; _snapRaw.cellId = player ? player.cellId >>> 0 : null; _snapRaw.coords = coordsText || null; _snapRaw.drawn = drawn; _snapRaw.valid = true;`. `drawn` is already a fresh per-tick array kept for hover (`blips = drawn`), so holding a reference costs nothing.
2. At mount, set a module-level `_snapFormat = () => ({ source, headingDeg: Math.round(heading*180/Math.PI*10)/10, range, cellId: hex or null, coords, tokens: read tokens[d].style now, blips: drawn.map(...same fields...), locked: !!winPos?.isLocked?.() })` that reads `_snapRaw` plus the closure's tokens and winPos.
3. `window.__radar.snapshot` becomes `() => (_snapFormat && _snapRaw.valid ? _snapFormat() : null)`. The JSON deep-copy is no longer needed because the formatter builds fresh objects, but keeping it is harmless.
4. Teardown sets `_snapFormat = null; _snapRaw.valid = false; _snapRaw.drawn = null;` in place of `_lastSnapshot = null`.
5. Keep the returned shape identical: {source, headingDeg, range, cellId, coords, tokens:{n,e,s,w}, blips:[{guid,name,x,y,shape,color,dist}], locked}. If radar-4 lands, add `blank`.
6. No flag is needed (debug-only and invisible).
Tests: `node test_radar_projection.mjs` (pure maths, unchanged). Optionally add a static assertion in tests/target_cycle.test.cjs (which already loads RADAR_SRC) that update() no longer contains `_lastSnapshot = {`. Live check by the orchestrator: `__radar.snapshot()` keeps the same keys. No wasm rebuild.
